descriptions.value: Traefik 3.7.11 before 3.7.15 contains an authorization bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider that skips the cross-namespace check on the auth-tls-secret annotation when a cached client authentication TLS option is reused. Users who can create Ingresses can reference another namespace's CA secret already used by another Ingress, enforcing it on their own routes and learning whether it exists, without disclosure of its contents.

cna.title: MariaDB Connector/J : XA recover() trusted server-supplied gtrid and bqual lengths

descriptions.value: MariaDB Connector/J is used to connect applications developed in Java to MariaDB and MySQL databases. From 3.0.0 until 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11, the MariaDbPoolConnection.recover() and MariaDbPoolPinnedConnection.recover() implementations trusted the gtrid_length and bqual_length columns returned by XA RECOVER. The methods allocated and split Xid byte arrays without validating the lengths against Xid.MAXGTRIDSIZE, Xid.MAXBQUALSIZE, or the actual data payload. A malicious or compromised server, or a machine-in-the-middle attacker, could cause large allocations, NegativeArraySizeException, or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException during XA recovery. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11.

cna.title: Gitea user and organization feed token scope bypass

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #40115

descriptions.value: The `/{username}` web route accepted personal access tokens over HTTP Basic authentication without checking their scope. A token confined to an unrelated scope, such as `read:issue`, could read its owner's private activity through the user RSS/Atom feed and the profile activity tab, and other members' activity in a private organization through the organization feed; a public-only token could list the owner's private repositories and organizations and render private profile READMEs. For a site administrator's token this applied to every account. Tokens are now accepted on this route only for feeds, which require `read:user` or `read:organization`.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH RTP Inject and RTP Bleed during auto adjustment, plus SRTP media denial of service

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. In 1.11.2 and earlier, rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c uses one session-wide autoadj_tally to learn RTP sources that differ from the address negotiated in SDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker who sends plaintext RTP during call setup can make packets from one or more non-advertised sources reach the threshold before the legitimate endpoint, causing FreeSWITCH to adopt the source of the threshold-crossing packet as the media peer. The attacker can then receive call audio, inject media, and deny media to the legitimate endpoint without being on the media path. FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 adds two opt-in controls, but both default to zero and the release remains affected unless both are configured before RTP session creation. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.11.2.

cna.title: Zuke: Resolved secret() values are written to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY in the clear, disclosing them to anyone who can view the workflow run

descriptions.value: Zuke is a code-first, strongly typed build automation system for Deno. Prior to 1.51.0, @zuke/core writes rendered reportSummary(...) notes to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY through writeJobSummary without applying the redactor that protects resolved secret() values in console and persisted run output. A GitHub Actions build that places secret-derived text in a summary note can publish credentials in cleartext to everyone able to view the workflow run, including unauthenticated viewers of a public repository, and the durable summary remains exposed until the run is deleted. GitHub Actions masking directives do not protect the summary file, while runs outside GitHub Actions and builds that do not summarize secret-derived text are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.51.0.

descriptions.value: The VobSub subtitle decoder libsub_vob (part of the Amlogic DroidLogic SubTitleService), as shipped on Nexbox A95X (Amlogic S905X) TV boxes, contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in vob_fill_pixel() that allows remote attackers to corrupt stack memory by sending a crafted SET_CONTR command with an attacker-controlled alpha value that drives an unbounded array index (change_data) past the end of the fixed four-element PixelDatas array. cna.title: MariaDB Connector/J: Rogue server can drive large heap allocations from server-declared lengths in OK packets

descriptions.value: MariaDB Connector/J is used to connect applications developed in Java to MariaDB and MySQL databases. From 3.0.0 until 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11, when CLIENT_SESSION_TRACK was negotiated, the OkPacket.parse() and OkPacket.parseWithInfo() paths allocated byte arrays using server-declared lengths for the OK packet info field and session-state variable names and values before confirming that the bytes remained in the packet. A malicious or compromised server, or a machine-in-the-middle attacker, could send a small OK packet declaring a much larger length and repeatedly force attacker-controlled heap allocations before the subsequent copy failed. This could create garbage-collection pressure or an OutOfMemoryError in the client application. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11.

descriptions.value: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instruction only after the entire literal had been received. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send an insert instruction on the QPACK encoder stream that declares an arbitrarily large literal and then keep sending data, causing the decoder to buffer it without bound for the lifetime of the connection and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service. The issue occurs regardless of the advertised QPACK dynamic table capacity, including when the dynamic table is disabled. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

cna.title: Welcart e-Commerce <= 2.12.5 - Account Takeover via Insecure Direct Object Reference to Unauthenticated User Input via 'member[ID]' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Welcart e-Commerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 2.12.5 via the 'member[ID]' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite any existing Welcart shop-member account's email address and password by supplying that member's numeric ID, then authenticate as that member to achieve full account takeover. The only authentication barrier is a wp_verify_nonce() check against a nonce printed to every unauthenticated visitor on the auto-published New Enrollment Form, meaning no existing account, no WordPress login, and no non-default configuration is required to exploit this vulnerability.

Attackers can supply a WITH clause chaining tens of thousands of CTEs, via plain SQL or a view in an untrusted database file, causing unbounded selectExpander() recursion that crashes the process.

descriptions.value: proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a frame of an unknown or reserved type, or a HEADERS frame, until its entire declared length had arrived, without limiting that length, and re-scanned all buffered data each time more bytes arrived. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could declare a very large frame and deliver it slowly, causing unbounded memory growth and CPU usage that grows quadratically with the number of fragments, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

cna.title: Incorrect authorization in issuer resolution in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes

descriptions.value: CAPEC-1 Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs

Incorrect authorization in the issuer resolution logic in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before v1.10.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, signed by a cluster-scoped AWS Private CA issuer that their approval policy does not authorize.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version v1.10.1 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.10.1-eksbuild.1, and update any certificate requests, Certificate resources, or Ingress annotations whose issuerRef.kind is missing, incorrect, or does not match the referenced issuer, since v1.10.1 requires issuerRef.kind to be exactly AWSPCAIssuer or AWSPCAClusterIssuer and to match the issuer it references.

cna.title: joserfc: Compact JWS size guard allocates attacker-controlled segments before rejection

descriptions.value: joserfc is a Python library that provides an implementation of several JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) standards. Prior to 1.7.6, joserfc compact JWS deserialization calls bytes.split() before enforcing the existing aggregate segment-size limits. When attacker-controlled compact serialization bytes reach deserialize_compact(), the split creates copies of the header, payload, and signature segments before ExceededSizeError rejects them, causing an additional allocation approximately proportional to the supplied token. Requests that exhaust available process memory can therefore cause an availability failure even though signature verification fails. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.6.

cna.title: Fluent Support <= 2.4.7 — Unauthenticated Limited Modification of Linked Customer Profile Fields via Fluent Forms Feed

affected.product: Fluent Support – Helpdesk & Customer Support Ticket System

descriptions.value: The Fluent Support – Helpdesk & Customer Support Ticket System plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated modification of a linked customer's stored profile fields in versions up to, and including, 2.4.7 Its first-party Fluent Forms integration (FeedIntegration::notify()) opens a ticket from each public form submission and, for a logged-out submitter, resolves the submitted email to an existing WordPress account via get_user_by('email', ...) without verifying the submitter controls that address, then passes the attacker-supplied data to Customer::maybeCreateCustomer(). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite a limited set of a registered customer's stored profile fields where an administrator has enabled a FluentSupport feed on a public form. The email address, role and status are never changed; first and last name are overwritten only when the target user has no name set in user meta; and other fields (title, address, city, state, zip, country) are writable only where an administrator has mapped them in the feed.

cna.title: Out-of-Bounds Read in Babelfish for PostgreSQL TDS RPC Procedure-Name Parser

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

An out-of-bounds read in the TDS RPC procedure-name parser in the Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 1.0-1.5, 2.1-2.15, 3.1-3.12, 4.0-4.8, 5.1-5.4 and in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish might allow remote authenticated users to read adjacent process memory or cause a denial of service via a malformed TDS RPC request to the TDS port (default 1433).



To remediate this issue, we recommend users upgrade to Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 4.10, 5.6, 6.1 or later. As a workaround, restrict network access to the TDS port (default 1433). Customers using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish should upgrade their cluster to Aurora PostgreSQL 13.9.16 (1.5.5), 13.23.3 (1.17.2), 14.6.16 (2.3.5), 14.17.8 (2.12.4), 14.18.6 (2.13.3), 14.19.5 (2.14.2), 14.20.5 (2.15.2), 14.22.3 (2.16.1), 14.23.1 (2.17.0), 15.10.8 (3.8.4), 15.12.8 (3.9.4), 15.13.6 (3.10.3), 15.14.5 (3.11.2), 15.15.5 (3.12.2), 15.17.3 (3.13.1), 15.18.1 (3.14.0), 16.8.8 (4.5.5), 16.9.6 (4.6.3), 16.10.5 (4.7.2), 16.11.5 (4.8.2), 16.13.3 (4.9.1), 16.14.1 (4.10.0), 17.4.8 (5.1.4), 17.5.6 (5.2.3), 17.6.5 (5.3.2), 17.7.5 (5.4.2), 17.9.3 (5.5.1), 17.10.1 (5.6.0), 18.3.4 (6.0.2), 18.4.1 (6.1.0) or later, and apply any pending maintenance to ensure they are on the latest patch.

cna.title: Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl complete redirect flows without checking the session token, letting a leaked redirect flow ID create payments against another customer's mandate

solutions.value: Upgrade to Business-GoCardless 1.01 or later.

descriptions.value:
Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl complete redirect flows without checking the session token, letting a leaked redirect flow ID create payments against another customer's mandate.

confirm_resource takes no session token from the caller. It reads the redirect flow back from the GoCardless API and completes it with the token from that response, so the check that the flow is completed by the session that started it always passes. It then creates the requested payment or subscription against the flow's mandate. Since version 1.00, a flow that already has a mandate is returned as confirmed without being completed again, so the same ID creates a new payment on every call.

A remote attacker who obtains another customer's redirect flow ID can create payments or subscriptions against that customer's mandate.

cna.title: TYPO3 CMS - Missing Authorization in Online Media Handling

descriptions.value:
The backend endpoint for adding online media (e.g. YouTube or Vimeo videos) accepted a target folder in the fallback storage (storage uid 0), which points to the public web root of the installation. File mount and permission checks are not applied to the fallback storage. As a result, any authenticated, low-privileged backend user, even without file mounts or module access, could create online media files with a partially controllable file name in the public web root.

In combination with TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-027, this could be used to re-enable the installer on an already configured instance. The installer could then be used to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution.

cna.title: Immich: Unauthenticated filesystem path injection (arbitrary directory write + recursive delete) in the machine-learning service

descriptions.value: Immich is a high-performance self-hosted photo and video management solution. Prior to 3.3.0, the unauthenticated machine-learning /predict endpoint in machine-learning/immich_ml/main.py accepted an options object and passed its values into model construction in machine-learning/immich_ml/models/base.py without restricting security-sensitive parameters. An attacker with network access to the service could set cache_dir to an arbitrary writable path, causing model downloads to write there and causing clear_cache() to pass that path to shutil.rmtree() after selected model-loading failures. Depending on filesystem permissions and the selected path, this could modify files in mounted data locations or recursively delete an attacker-selected directory. The model-name allowlist prevents this issue from becoming arbitrary-model deserialization or code execution. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.0.

cna.title: croc: Overwrite-confirmation bypass via a crafted "croc-stdin-" filename on receive

descriptions.description: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

descriptions.value: croc is a tool that allows any two computers to simply and securely transfer files and folders. Prior to 11.5.2, the receive-side file-readiness loop in src/croc/croc.go treats any sender-controlled basename beginning with croc-stdin- as a trusted text-transfer artifact even when SendingText is false. This skips askReceiveOverwrite and rename handling for a predictable exact-name collision in the receiver's working directory, allowing a remote sender whose transfer the user accepts to overwrite or truncate a matching regular file through recipientInitializeFile, or to remove and replace a matching destination with an empty file or an in-directory symlink through createEmptyFileAndFinish, without confirmation. The impact is limited to pre-existing names in the croc-stdin- namespace that the sender can predict; other filenames retain the prompt, dotfiles outside that namespace are not reachable, and symlink targets remain confined to the receive directory. This issue is fixed in version 11.5.2.

cna.title: Gstreamer1-plugins-good: gstreamer1-plugins-good: out-of-bounds heap read in mtap16/mtap24 h.264 rtp depayloader via signed/unsigned underflow

credits.value: Upstream acknowledges Ada Logics (Ada Logics) and Claude (Anthropic) as the original reporters.

workarounds.value: Block untrusted H.264 RTP streams at the network perimeter (firewall or UDP ingress filter) to prevent malformed packets from reaching GStreamer pipelines. Alternatively, disable or avoid deploying the rtph264depay GStreamer element when processing RTP from untrusted sources.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-good, specifically in the H.264 RTP depayloader element. When processing MTAP16 or MTAP24 multi-time aggregation RTP packets, a signed/unsigned integer conversion error causes the remaining-length counter to underflow to a large positive value when the packet is truncated. This allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds heap read of up to approximately 64 KiB of process memory by sending a single malformed RTP packet. Successful exploitation can crash the receiving GStreamer pipeline (denial of service), and in relay or transcoding deployments where output is accessible to the attacker, may expose adjacent heap contents.

descriptions.value: The Content Egg – Affiliate Product Importer & Price Comparison plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 12.0.0 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to create posts attributed to another user's account — typically an administrator — by supplying an admin-owned preset_id, causing wp_insert_post to record the administrator as post_author. cna.title: GraphQL-core: Denial of service via memory leak in aborted validations

descriptions.description: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

descriptions.value: GraphQL-core is a Python port of the GraphQL.js reference implementation. From 3.3.0a3 until 3.3.1, validate() reuses a module-level ValidationAbortedError when a document exceeds max_errors. Python appends frames to the reused exception's traceback on every raise, retaining each document, validation context, and error set for the process lifetime. An unauthenticated client can repeatedly submit a small document with more than 100 validation errors to cause unbounded memory growth before query execution, eventually exhausting worker memory without disclosing or modifying data. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.1.

cna.title: Zuke: githubWorkflow adopts any workflow run whose title matches its marker, so anyone who can dispatch the workflow can satisfy or block a release gate

descriptions.value: Zuke is a code-first, strongly typed build automation system for Deno. Prior to 1.10.0, the @zuke/gh githubWorkflow(...) gate correlates a dispatched workflow run using only a display-title marker that is visible in the workflow run list and can be copied by another dispatcher. In configurations where the external workflow repository grants workflow_dispatch permission to a party not equally trusted by the releasing repository, an attacker can dispatch a run with the marker and cause the gate to adopt its conclusion without verifying the event, ref, or creation window. A passing substituted run can authorize an unvalidated release, while a failed or cancelled run can block a valid release, and the persisted adopted run ID preserves the substitution across build resume. This issue is fixed in version 1.10.0.

An attacker who can modify the attester's workload code, memory-backed state, configuration, or attached devices after that check can keep the existing connection open while the peer continues trusting stale initial Evidence. This gap is especially significant for long-lived connections because the verifier has no mechanism to detect the changed state. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

cna.title: Nx: OS command injection via nx.json plugin options in @nx/maven and @nx/gradle

descriptions.value: Nx is a monorepo solution for TypeScript and polyglot codebases. From 22.0.2 until 22.7.9 and 23.1.2 for @nx/maven, and from 21.0.0 until 22.7.9 and 23.1.2 for @nx/gradle, the plugins' project-graph analyzers launch through a shell and interpolate plugin options from nx.json into command arguments. The @nx/maven targetNamePrefix value and arbitrary @nx/gradle option names or values can therefore be interpreted as shell syntax whenever an nx command constructs the project graph. A user who runs Nx in an attacker-controlled repository or pull request can execute injected commands with the user's privileges, while workspaces that register neither affected plugin are not exposed to this path. Remediation requires upgrading both nx and each affected plugin to matching releases because the plugin fix depends on code in the nx package. This issue is fixed in versions 22.7.9 and 23.1.2.

descriptions.value: Tesseract is an open source OCR engine. From 5.4.0 until 5.5.4, AppendLinePolygon in src/api/pagerenderer.cpp destroys the caller-owned right-to-left Pta accumulator while receiving it by value, leaving line_top_rtl_pts and line_bottom_rtl_pts dangling. On an upright Hebrew or Arabic page at the default PAGE XML level, POLYGONFLAG with a false skewed_flag enters the vulnerable calls, while LEVELFLAG greater than zero provides an alternative gate. The calls repeatedly read and free the stale object, causing a double free and use after free and allowing corrupted coordinates to reach RecalcPolygonline. This issue is fixed in version 5.5.4.

descriptions.value: The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' merge-tag of the [ghr] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 4.10 The post_title replacement is registered with 'nested' => true, so the nested branch of Replacements::do_replacement() returns the merge value through tackle_replacements() without passing it through escape_merge_tags()/escape_shortcodes(); the callback single_post() calls html_entity_decode(get_the_title(), ENT_QUOTES), converting the entity-encoded text that wp_filter_kses leaves intact on a Contributor's post title back into raw HTML, which is then emitted into the rendered post. cna.title: Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by flattening legacy webhook payloads before checking their signature

solutions.value: Upgrade to Business-GoCardless 1.01 or later.

descriptions.value:
Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by flattening legacy webhook payloads before checking their signature.

A webhook body with a top-level "payload" key is verified as a legacy webhook. To rebuild the signed string, the payload is flattened into one key and value pair per leaf, each key carrying the full path to that leaf, and the pairs are then encoded, sorted and joined. A long key holding a long array costs memory proportional to the key length times the array length.

A remote attacker can exhaust memory in the process receiving webhooks with a single request that carries no valid signature.

cna.title: Forge: AES-GCM authentication bypass via unvalidated tagLength option

descriptions.value: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, node-forge did not validate the AES-GCM tagLength option passed to start() during decryption through forge.cipher.createDecipher(). When an application derived tagLength from received data or used an unset or zero-like configuration value, a value that converted to zero together with an empty or missing authentication tag caused the calculated and supplied tags to compare as empty, so decipher.finish() accepted unauthenticated ciphertext. Applications that omit tagLength to use the 128-bit default or pass a fixed valid tag length are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

cna.title: mongofiles may disclose GridFS content to standard output through a stored filename

descriptions.value: MongoDB Database Tools mongofiles uses a database-stored GridFS filename as the output destination for get_id when --local is not specified. A user who can modify the file metadata can set the stored filename to '-', causing a later authorized retrieval to write the file contents to standard output instead of a local file. If standard output is captured in a location accessible to that user, this may disclose GridFS content the user cannot read directly. Exploitation requires a higher-privileged operator to retrieve the affected file without an explicit local destination and attacker access to the captured output. This issue affects MongoDB Database Tools from version 3.1.4 through versions before 100.20.1.

cna.title: Ladybird: FinalizationRegistry::cleanup() heap use-after-free via reentrant unregister()

descriptions.value: Ladybird is a truly independent web browser. Prior to 209579c96473c75bd5eba9701fcadb841a045964, FinalizationRegistry::cleanup() in Libraries/LibJS/Runtime/FinalizationRegistry.cpp removed a dead record from m_records, retained an iterator to the next FinalizationRecord, and then invoked attacker-controlled JavaScript through the cleanup callback. If that callback called unregister() for the next record, remove_by_token() freed the node referenced by the retained iterator, and the next cleanup iteration read its target and held_value fields after free. This reliably crashes instrumented WebContent builds and creates a memory-corruption primitive in production builds. This vulnerability is fixed by commit 209579c96473c75bd5eba9701fcadb841a045964.

Attackers can retrieve resources fetched with another caller's credentials or from URLs that a later document's access policy would deny, resulting in cross-document information disclosure and bypass of the URL access policy.

cna.title: Wekan: ReDoS via Unescaped User Input in RegExp

descriptions.value: Wekan is open source kanban built with Meteor. Prior to 11.11, the user-search publication in server/publications/users.js and the searchUsers method in server/models/users.js pass authenticated user-controlled searchTerm and query values to new RegExp() without escaping regular-expression metacharacters. MongoDB-backed deployments evaluate the resulting patterns with PCRE2, allowing a logged-in user to submit catastrophic-backtracking expressions that consume database CPU and degrade or deny service to other users; searchUsers additionally requires board membership or site-admin status. The FerretDB v1 / RE2 unaffected configuration is not practically affected by catastrophic backtracking. This issue is fixed in version 11.11.

cna.title: MariaDB Connector/J: Rogue server can crash the client during caching_sha2_password authentication

cna.title: zuke setup and zuke import follow symbolic links planted at scaffold names, allowing writes outside the target directory

descriptions.value: Zuke is a code-first, strongly typed build automation system for Deno. Prior to 1.4.0, @zuke/cli uses lstat to inspect scaffold names but then performs link-following reads, writes, and permission changes in zuke setup and zuke import. An attacker who supplies an untrusted cloned repository, template, or archive with a symbolic link at a scaffolded name can cause setup to overwrite a target outside the selected directory with the invoking user's permissions. The .gitignore path requires no flag, while --force permits a linked launcher target to be written and made executable; import can also read link-target content and incorporate it into the generated build file. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

cna.title: libp2p: gossipsub creates a permanent topics-map entry per distinct subscription with no cap in the default config

descriptions.value: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 17.0.0, the @libp2p/gossipsub default configuration allows a connected remote peer to submit unsigned subscription RPC metadata for arbitrarily many distinct topic strings. handleReceivedSubscription in packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts creates a persistent topics-map entry for each accepted topic, while allowedTopics is unset by default, decodeRpc maxSubscriptions limits only one RPC rather than aggregate topic bytes, and peer scoring has no subscription-volume penalty. A single peer can therefore grow the topics map and committed heap toward out-of-memory conditions, and disconnecting additionally causes removePeer to scan all accumulated topic entries. This issue is fixed in version 17.0.0.

cna.title: User Frontend <= 4.3.14 - Authenticated (Author+) Privilege Escalation to 'post_content' Parameter

affected.product: User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission

descriptions.value: The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.14 via the `draft_post()` function. This is due to the function storing the `post_content` parameter via `wp_insert_post()` without the protected-shortcode allow-list check that was introduced in 4.3.14 for the sibling `submit_post()` handler — a gap that `wp_kses` filtering does not close, as it strips only HTML tags while leaving shortcode text such as `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` intact. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to embed a registration shortcode in a post and cause any site visitor who subsequently registers through the rendered form to receive Editor-level access. The render-time `wpuf_modify_shortcodes` filter that is designed to neutralize protected shortcodes provides no protection here because posts created via the `wpuf_draft_post` AJAX endpoint carry no `_edit_last` post meta, causing the filter to return the content unchanged and allowing the shortcode to render and execute fully.

descriptions.value: The Reset Database plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to privilege escalation in versions up to, and including, 1.1.3. This is due to the process_reset() function being registered on admin_init with no capability check, a computed-but-unused nonce, a gating condition that passes whenever no WordPress administrator literally named 'admin' exists (the default on modern installs), and an identity test that verifies the ATTACKER'S OWN password rather than an administrator's. descriptions.value: An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or Handshake) that the TLS handshake had already moved past. Because the transport treated this data as delivered, it did not count against the CRYPTO stream buffer limit. A remote, unauthenticated client could complete a handshake, withhold its acknowledgment of the server's HANDSHAKE_DONE frame so that Handshake keys stay in use, and keep sending Handshake-level CRYPTO data at increasing offsets, causing unbounded memory growth on the server and leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

cna.title: joserfc: Unbounded JWE General JSON `recipients` Array Leads to CPU Exhaustion (DoS) via Repeated RSA Private-Key Decryption

descriptions.value: joserfc is a Python library that provides an implementation of several JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) standards. Prior to 1.7.5, joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json() accepts a JWE General JSON Serialization recipients array without a count limit and calls decrypt_cek() for every entry. An unauthenticated attacker who can submit a JWE to an endpoint using an RSA key-management algorithm can choose the number of private-key decryption operations performed by one request. The verify_all_recipients option does not reduce this work because the affected loop processes every recipient before consulting that setting, allowing repeated requests to exhaust service CPU without affecting confidentiality or integrity. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.5.

cna.title: Next.js: Cache poisoning of shared fallback shells in Cache Components via request-supplied placeholder route params

descriptions.value: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.4.0 until 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js applications served with next start can allow an unauthenticated request to poison a shared fallback shell when cacheComponents is true and partialPrefetching is unset or false. The affected dynamic route must have a prerenderable param declared by generateStaticParams whose requested value was not generated at build time, at least two never-prerenderable params below it, a layout that reads the shallower param inside a Suspense boundary, and a blocking fallback shell. A request-supplied placeholder route param whose path segment equals the percent-encoded bracketed name of its own deeper route param is incorrectly treated as unresolved, while the shallower concrete value is rendered into the shared shell and its HTTP status is persisted. Depending on application behavior, subsequent routes sharing that shell can receive a persistent 404 or attacker-selected substituted param text. Client hydration corrects substituted text, and the issue does not enable markup or script injection or disclose data. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

This issue is fixed in version 6.5.

An application configured with a wildcard-subdomain AllowOrigins value and AllowCredentials enabled can reflect an unrelated attacker-controlled origin whose host merely ends with the configured base domain. A user who visits that origin can expose authenticated cross-origin responses to the attacker's page; empty-label origins and later comma-space parsing hardening are outside this advisory. cna.title: Forge: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery via non-canonical DigestInfo encoding

descriptions.value: Forge, also called node-forge, is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, publicKey.verify() with the default RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5 scheme in lib/rsa.js parses the recovered DigestInfo with the lenient BER parser asn1.fromDer() and validates its structure with digestInfoValidator without requiring canonical DER bytes. Non-minimal or indefinite lengths, malformed parameter values, and non-canonical object identifier encodings with padded subidentifiers or trailing bytes can leave attacker-controlled data inside an accepted DigestInfo. When the verifying RSA public key uses a low exponent such as e=3, an attacker can use that encoding slack to forge a signature without the private key. The same path is used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 signature verification. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

descriptions.description: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

cna.title: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum

scenarios.value:
AV:L - A malicious microVM supplies crafted virtio-net checksum metadata with its outbound frame. The VMM writes it to the host TAP, where tun_get_user() feeds the skb to the IPv4 stack and ip_do_fragment() calls skb_checksum_help(); this is a guest/local virtual-device path, not an Internet receive path.
AC:L - The guest controls the frame, checksum start and offset, and packet size and can repeat the same fragmentation sequence. No race, timing window, or uncontrollable memory layout is needed; host leak, crash, and code-execution variants were reproduced with crafted packets.
PR:N - In the microVM scenario, a tenant workload able to transmit through its assigned virtio-net interface can supply the triggering traffic. It needs no host credentials, capability, or access to /dev/net/tun; the privileged VMM merely forwards guest output to its existing TAP fd.
UI:N - The attacker sends the crafted guest packets directly, and host TAP/IPv4 processing invokes checksum completion automatically. No host administrator or other victim must act.
S:C - The checksum metadata originates in an untrusted microVM, but skb_checksum_help() and ip_do_fragment() process and corrupt state in the host kernel. The demonstrated leak, crash, and administrator code execution cross the guest-to-host isolation boundary.
C:H - After skb_checksum_help() changes an already-validated IPv4 IHL, ip_do_fragment() trusts the new length and ip_frag_next() copies beyond the skb's logical linear head into transmitted IPv4 options. This was demonstrated as continuous host-memory disclosure in guest-emitted packets.
I:H - skb_checksum_help() writes at the attacker-controlled checksum position inside an IPv4 header after routing and validation, and downstream code trusts the modified fields. Crafted guest packets using this flaw were demonstrated to execute commands with full administrator privileges on the host.
A:H - Malformed checksum offsets reach skb_checksum_help() from IPv4 fragmentation and can trip WARN_ONCE/panic paths or poison the header geometry used downstream. Crafted guest packets were demonstrated to crash the physical host, taking down all sandboxes on it.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum

If a packet with bad checksum metadata gets into the ipv4 stack,
skb_checksum_help can corrupt the network header and cause a bunch of
mischief.

This was discovered and reported by Paulos, and has been reporoduced
by others independently since.

We really shouldn't allow such packets in, but as a defence
in depth measure, let's also check before we complete the checksum.

A more complete validation at input is forthcoming, but needs more work.

descriptions.description: CWE-362 Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

cna.title: inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups

scenarios.value:
AV:N - IPv4/IPv6 TCP segments reach the patched lookups from tcp_v4_rcv via __inet_lookup_skb and from tcp_v6_rcv via __inet6_lookup_skb. A SYN-cookie ACK in cookie_v4_check makes tcp_get_cookie_sock publish a refcount on an unhashed request of that 4-tuple, which the racing established lookup returns.
AC:L - The attacker overflows the listener SYN queue so default tcp_syncookies=1 enters cookie_v4_check, then sends that cookie ACK together with a concurrent segment for the same 4-tuple; request_sock reuse is driven by those packets, and the reported PoC reproduced the oops.
PR:N - cookie_v4_check and tcp_v4_rcv handle the ACK in the receive softirq before accept and before TCP-MD5/AO or any other credential check, so the sender needs no account or capability.
UI:N - The attacker alone sends the SYN flood and the cookie ACK to a socket that is already listening; no mount, open, or other victim action is required.
S:U - The fault is in the host kernel's tcp_v4_rcv softirq and panics that same kernel; it does not cross a guest/host or sandbox boundary.
C:N - tcp_v4_rcv reads sk_state through req->rsk_listener, which cookie_tcp_reqsk_alloc left NULL by calling inet_reqsk_alloc with attach_listener false; the faulting address is the constant 0x12 and no socket bytes are returned to the peer.
I:N - On the path that oopses, the lookup returns the still-live cookie request and tcp_v4_rcv faults on the NULL listener before tcp_check_req or any write to socket, packet, or connection state.
A:H - The NULL sk_state read is in softirq inside tcp_v4_rcv, reached from ip_protocol_deliver_rcu, and the reported result is a fatal exception panic ("Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt").

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups

TCP established ehash lookups are lockless. The socket caches involved
use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU, so memory can be reused before an RCU reader
that retained its old address has finished.

After a tuple match, __inet_lookup_established() and
__inet6_lookup_established() acquire a reference and repeat the tuple
check. They do not check whether the new object is hashed. If the
address is reused for a socket with the same tuple, the lookup can
acquire a reference to the new object and return it while its nulls node
is unhashed.

A PoC that drives reuse with a SYN cookie request socket reproduced the
crash. The new request socket is unhashed and has a NULL rsk_listener.
A lookup that had loaded the address of the old request socket acquired
the reference published by tcp_get_cookie_sock() and returned the new
object. tcp_v4_rcv() then read sk_state through the NULL listener.

The resulting crash was:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000012
  #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
  #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
  ...
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 4 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/4 Not tainted 7.3.0-00591-g0e135910deec #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  ...
  RIP: 0010:tcp_v4_rcv+0x44e/0x1280
  ...
  R10: 0000000000000001 R11: 00000000024ca8c0 R12: 0000000000000000
  ...
  CR2: 0000000000000012 CR3: 0000000103d50004 CR4: 0000000000770ef0
  ...
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   ? raw_local_deliver+0xae/0x240
   ip_protocol_deliver_rcu+0x2d/0x180
   ip_local_deliver_finish+0x84/0x100
   ip_sublist_rcv_finish+0x5f/0x70
   ip_sublist_rcv+0x12a/0x1d0
   ip_list_rcv+0xfd/0x130
   __netif_receive_skb_list_core+0x223/0x250
   netif_receive_skb_list_internal+0x1d2/0x2c0
   ? try_fill_recv+0x39/0x7b0
   napi_complete_done+0x74/0x170
   virtnet_poll+0x445/0x600
   __napi_poll+0x27/0x1e0
   net_rx_action+0x2fe/0x3b0
   handle_softirqs+0xc2/0x2c0
   __irq_exit_rcu+0x74/0xd0
   common_interrupt+0x7f/0x90
   </IRQ>
  ...
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

After taking a reference, check whether the nulls node is unhashed in
both IPv4 and IPv6 established lookups. If it is unhashed or the tuple
no longer matches, drop the reference and restart the lookup.

Lookups racing with the TIME_WAIT hashdance, or with a request being
replaced by its child, now restart and find the new socket instead of
returning the old one.

Request sockets that were never inserted into ehash can have a nonzero
refcount, and a stale lookup can hold a transient reference. Therefore,
when SYN cookie, Fast Open, and request migration paths fail after
setting a nonzero refcount, release the references held by those paths
with reqsk_put() instead of freeing the request directly.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 sets the alarm receiver state to waiting for confirmation before the data of a received alarm notification is parsed. cna.title: Unbounded Memory Retention in QUIC Server for Rejected Streams

descriptions.value:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-1 Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs

Incorrect default file permissions in Kiro CLI (formerly Amazon Q Developer CLI) before version 2.27.0 on macOS and Linux might allow other local users on the same host to read a user's session transcripts and prompt history, including any credentials or source code they contain. cna.title: @fastify/multipart vulnerable to arbitrary file write via type confusion in saveRequestFiles()

descriptions.value: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 7.4.0 through 10.1.8, when the plugin is registered with the attachFieldsToBody option, the saveRequestFiles helper treats any object in the parsed request body that carries truthy file and buffer properties as an uploaded file. An unauthenticated client can forge such an object through a plain JSON request or a JSON-typed multipart field, so attacker-chosen bytes are written to the temporary directory while upload hooks and the file count and size limits are skipped, and the saved entry keeps the attacker's filename verbatim instead of being reduced to its basename. Because that filename can contain parent directory segments, applications that use it as a write destination, as the project README example does, are exposed to an arbitrary relative-path file write from a single request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.9, and users should upgrade to 10.1.9 or later. As a workaround, call saveRequestFiles only after confirming the request is multipart, and reduce each returned filename to its basename or validate it against an allowlist before using it as a destination.

cna.title: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to Denial of Service via truncated multipart part past the parts limit

descriptions.value: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, when a request reaches the configured limit on the number of multipart parts, each further part is skipped without attaching an error listener to the skipped part stream. If the request body ends in the middle of such a skipped part, the vendored Dicer parser emits an error on that stream, and because nothing is listening Node.js raises an unhandled error event and the process exits. A single crafted unauthenticated request is therefore enough to crash the server. The bug is latent in the parser on its own and was first demonstrated through @fastify/multipart versions 10.1.2 through 10.1.4, which keep feeding the request body to the parser after a limit error, and it affects any consumer that sets a finite parts limit and parses request bodies that can be terminated early. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. There is no complete application level workaround because the crash happens inside the parser before application code runs, though consumers that set a finite parts limit should also attach an error listener to the parser stream.

cna.title: Apache Axis2/C: Out-of-bounds read in the Guththila XML reader wrapper

descriptions.value: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the Guththila XML parser wrapper of Apache Axis2/C. On some malformed XML input the Guththila parser returned a raw input byte in place of an event code, and the AXIOM reader wrapper used that value as an index into a ten-entry lookup table without checking its range, reading heap memory past the end of the table. An unauthenticated client could trigger this by sending a crafted XML request to a server built with Guththila, the default parser, causing the request to be parsed incorrectly or, in some cases, the process to crash. The memory read is not returned to the client. This issue affects Apache Axis2/C: through 2.0.0. The fix is available in commits 23110287924e79d05a5b4712298c355d1f05c606 and f01683ec10e8fddb87279ec9351b3239021223e6 and will be included in the next release.

On some malformed XML input the Guththila parser returned a raw input byte in place of an event code, and the AXIOM reader wrapper used that value as an index into a ten-entry lookup table without checking its range, reading heap memory past the end of the table. An unauthenticated client could trigger this by sending a crafted XML request to a server built with Guththila, the default parser, causing the request to be parsed incorrectly or, in some cases, the process to crash. The memory read is not returned to the client. This issue affects Apache Axis2/C: through 2.0.0. The fix is available in commits 23110287924e79d05a5b4712298c355d1f05c606 and f01683ec10e8fddb87279ec9351b3239021223e6 and will be included in the next release.

descriptions.value: Phison E12 and E18 PCIe SSD controllers contain a Secure Boot bypass vulnerability that allows a privileged local attacker to inject persistent boot-patch tuples into the unsigned, CRC-protected flash ID page read by the BootROM. By overwriting a fuse-derived RAM variable via a crafted patch entry using Phison Vendor Specific Commands, an attacker can force CRC-only firmware verification instead of signature checking, enabling an unsigned firmware image to load and creating a persistent controller-level implant that survives firmware reinstallation and operates below the host operating system.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-139 Relative Path Traversal

The export-cluster-logs and export-image-logs commands in the AWS ParallelCluster CLI before version 3.16.0 contain a relative path traversal issue. An authenticated remote user with write access to the log export Amazon S3 bucket could use a crafted S3 object key to write files outside the intended export directory on the machine running the command. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 3.16.0 or later.

The set_post_metas() method  calls maybe_unserialize() on attacker-controlled postmeta string values parsed from the uploaded JSON import file. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP Objects. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that the site has enable_instructor_registration=true AND enable_guest_checkout=true AND at least one purchasable course exists. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

descriptions.value: NASA JPL ION-DTN 2.2.1b through 4.2.0 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the Datagram Retransmission (DGR) convergence layer that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a maliciously crafted 64-bit svcDataLength value that wraps a 32-bit allocation size calculation. references.name: Path bindings ignored for gRPC Content-Types on transcoded routes in elixir-grpc grpc_server

descriptions.value:
Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows an attacker to make a handler act on a resource other than the one named in the URL of an HTTP-transcoded route, via a request with a gRPC Content-Type.

Only the transcoding clause of GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server.ex, and lib/grpc/server.ex before the package split) applies the route's path bindings to the request message. The Cowboy handler picks that clause from the request Content-Type, not from the route. A request to a transcoded URL with application/grpc or application/grpc-web is decoded from the body alone, so every path-bound field takes its value from the body. A gateway, proxy rule or WAF that authorizes on the URL path sees one resource while the handler receives another.

This issue affects grpc: from 0.8.0 before 1.0.0; grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

1. Start a server with `http_transcode: true` and a transcoded route that binds a field from the path, for example `GET /v1/messages/{name}`.
2. Build a gRPC frame whose message sets `name` to `victim`.
3. Send it over HTTP/1.1 as `GET /v1/messages/alice` with `Content-Type: application/grpc`.
4. Observe that the handler receives `name` set to `victim`, not `alice`.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. The header selects the clause

The Cowboy handler derives the access mode from the request Content-Type. application/json selects :http_transcoding, application/grpc selects :grpc and application/grpc-web+proto selects :grpcweb. The router still matches the transcoded URL template and extracts its path bindings.

2. Bindings are applied in one clause only

GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 reads the bindings with adapter.get_bindings/1 and merges them through GRPC.Server.Transcode.map_request/5 only in the :http_transcoding clause. The unary and request-streaming clauses decode the body alone with the selected codec. GRPC.Codec.Proto is in the default codecs of every server, so application/grpc is always accepted.

3. The HTTP/1.1 guard never matches

resolve_access_mode/3 has a clause that forces transcoding for HTTP/1.1 requests. It matches the version as the binary "HTTP/1.1", while Cowboy stores the version as an atom, so the clause never applies and the request works over plain HTTP/1.1.

4. Result

A request to /v1/messages/alice with Content-Type: application/grpc and a message that sets name to victim reaches the handler with name set to victim. With an empty message the field is empty: the path binding is never consulted.

The Cowboy handler derives the access mode from the request `Content-Type`. `application/json` selects `:http_transcoding`, `application/grpc` selects `:grpc` and `application/grpc-web+proto` selects `:grpcweb`. The router still matches the transcoded URL template and extracts its path bindings.

**2. Bindings are applied in one clause only**

`GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4` reads the bindings with `adapter.get_bindings/1` and merges them through `GRPC.Server.Transcode.map_request/5` only in the `:http_transcoding` clause. The unary and request-streaming clauses decode the body alone with the selected codec. `GRPC.Codec.Proto` is in the default codecs of every server, so `application/grpc` is always accepted.

**3. The HTTP/1.1 guard never matches**

`resolve_access_mode/3` has a clause that forces transcoding for HTTP/1.1 requests. It matches the version as the binary `"HTTP/1.1"`, while Cowboy stores the version as an atom, so the clause never applies and the request works over plain HTTP/1.1.

**4. Result**

A request to `/v1/messages/alice` with `Content-Type: application/grpc` and a message that sets `name` to `victim` reaches the handler with `name` set to `victim`. With an empty message the field is empty: the path binding is never consulted.

cna.title: Busybox: heap buffer overflow in the tftp client on fallback to the default block size

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Duc Anh Luu for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When the TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) client requests a custom small block size and receives a standard response, it falls back to the default block size without resizing the allocated memory buffer. A malicious TFTP server can exploit this issue by sending standard-sized network packets during a transfer, causing a heap buffer overflow. This flaw allows an attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the application.

cna.title: Busybox: httpd password rule bypass for pre-compressed .gz files via accept-encoding: gzip

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Duc Anh Luu for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
To mitigate this vulnerability without modifying binary features, apply one of the following configuration measures:

1. Configure directory-level authentication:
In the BusyBox `httpd.conf` configuration file, define authentication rules covering the containing directory rather than individual file paths. Directory rules are evaluated against both the base request and served compressed variants.

2. Protect base filenames:
When individual file protection is necessary, configure password rules for both the uncompressed filename and the `.gz` filename (for example, applying the directive to both `/secret.txt` and `/secret.txt.gz`).

3. Restrict service access:
Restrict network reachability to the BusyBox httpd daemon using local firewall rules if remote access is not required.

Warning: Applying changes to httpd.conf requires restarting or reloading the BusyBox httpd process, which will temporarily terminate active network sessions.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When the HTTP daemon (httpd) has pre-compressed file support enabled, authentication checks are evaluated only against the requested URL path rather than the pre-compressed file being served. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by requesting an uncompressed file path while specifying gzip encoding, bypassing password rules configured specifically for the compressed file. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized information disclosure of sensitive files.

descriptions.description: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel

descriptions.value: plist.js (npm package 'plist') before 5.0.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the binary property-list parser (parseBinary) that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash a Node.js process by exploiting unmemoized recursive resolution of shared object references for arrays and dictionaries. Attackers can craft a small binary plist (under 200 bytes) containing chained self-referencing object indices to trigger exponential (2^N) resolution calls and memory growth, causing an unrecoverable out-of-memory crash and denial of service.

cna.title: Flexible PDF Invoices for WooCommerce & WordPress <= 7.1.2 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Billing Field

affected.product: Flexible PDF Invoices for WooCommerce & WordPress

descriptions.value: The Flexible PDF Invoices for WooCommerce & WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.first_name / extensions.wpdesk-flexible-invoices-checkout._billing_vat_number' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution requires an administrator to open the invoice edit page for the attacker's order and interact with (e.g., type into or trigger a change/keyup event on) a field in the customer metabox, at which point the payload stored in billing fields such as first_name or _billing_vat_number is decoded from its entity-escaped input value and passed unsanitized to jQuery .html(). Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

cna.title: `http.cookiejar` applies expired `Set-Cookie` to cookie store before policy validation

descriptions.value:
http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response carried an
already expired Set-Cookie header for it, using the Domain and Path
attributes from the header without consulting the cookie policy. A server
could therefore delete cookies belonging to other domains from a shared
cookie jar, such as the one used by urllib's HTTPCookieProcessor. The fix
consults the cookie policy before an expired cookie may delete an existing
one, as required by RFC 6265 section 5.3.

Eclipse Langium versions 3.2.0 through 4.4.0 contain an inefficient algorithmic complexity issue (CWE-407) in the opt-in IndentationAwareTokenBuilder and IndentationAwareLexer. When producing DEDENT tokens, the token builder recomputes line numbers by re-scanning the entire preceding document text. A document whose indentation changes on most lines then takes quadratic time to tokenize. Because tokenization is synchronous, a crafted document of a few hundred kilobytes can block the Node.js event loop for tens of seconds. That causes a DoS for every user served by the same process. Languages built with the DefaultLexer and DefaultTokenBuilder are unaffected.

cna.title: A DCP Set of the IP suite that is refused is still stored

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 copies the IP suite of a DCP Set request to the current and the non-volatile configuration, and starts saving it, before the state of the device is checked. If the request is refused, for example because an Application Relationship is active, the configuration is not restored and is still saved. After a restart the device uses the refused address, and may not answer the controller or may use its address. A host with ADJACENT network access can use this while an Application Relationship is active.

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str.

A string is decoded through a fixed-size buffer (16 KiB in 4.04), and each time the buffer fills its contents move into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the string is then rejected for a control character, an invalid escape, malformed UTF-8 or the end of the input.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains the decoded part of each rejected string, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

descriptions.description: CWE-401 Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
CWE-120 Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')

cna.title: Busybox: httpd stack buffer overflow via an "i:" rule in a subdirectory httpd.conf

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Duc Anh Luu for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Prevent untrusted users from creating or modifying configuration files by restricting write permissions on all web root and subdirectory paths served by BusyBox httpd to administrative accounts only:

chmod -R o-w /path/to/webroot

Additionally, ensure the BusyBox httpd process drops elevated privileges by specifying an unprivileged user with the `-u` flag upon execution:

busybox httpd -u nobody

Restarting the daemon is required for process-level flag changes to take effect, which will temporarily terminate active network connections.

Caveats: Running under a non-privileged user account prevents binding directly to privileged ports (below 1024) without additional system capabilities or port forwarding, and restricting directory permissions may interfere with workflows that require unprivileged file uploads.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When the httpd web server processes subdirectory configuration files, an overly long index page name can trigger a stack-based buffer overflow. An attacker with permissions to write to a subdirectory configuration file could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges or cause a denial of service (DoS) by crashing the server process.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size after a NUL byte in incr_parse

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size after a NUL byte in incr_parse.

The parser appends each chunk to its buffer and compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. It treats a NUL byte as the end of the input, so a NUL within the first max_size bytes keeps it short of the limit. The buffer keeps growing, and incr_skip cannot remove the NUL.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer can exhaust process memory regardless of max_size.

descriptions.value: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.9, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware with a matcher that requires a non-empty value for a dynamic segment, while Fastify's router accepts an empty parameter or wildcard value. When a route and an Express middleware mount share a dynamic pattern, a request with an empty segment matches the Fastify route and runs the handler while the middleware mounted on that pattern is skipped, so on a scoped mount an unauthenticated request can reach a protected handler. No special configuration is required, and the practical impact depends on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

affected.product: Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization

descriptions.value: The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the replace_urls_in_value function in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.19. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires PEAR's Archive_Tar library to be present and loadable on the host (common in official WordPress Docker images and many PHP distributions), and an administrator must subsequently use the plugin's Rename control on any attachment after the attacker has staged a malicious payload in a comment. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

descriptions.value: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in Samsung Escargot 5.0.2 in the buffer-access paths for ReloadableString and CompressibleString. Internal raw character accessors and the public StringRef::stringBufferAccessData() API did not preserve the lifetime of the underlying buffer while it remained in use. As a result, idle unloading or garbage-collection compression could release the buffer and leave a stale pointer. Subsequent access may cause the process to crash or, under allocation-dependent conditions, expose limited contents of another heap allocation. The issue was addressed by adding buffer-lifetime reference tracking and removing unsafe raw character accessors.

cna.title: SQL Injection in Database Migration via Stored Connector Identifiers in flowintel

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [security] Bind stored connector identifiers during

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [security] Bind stored connector identifiers during
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The vulnerability is remediated by replacing direct string interpolation of stored database values into SQL queries with parameterized (bound) queries, ensuring that user-supplied or stored data is treated strictly as data rather than executable SQL. Additionally, the NULL handling for identifier fields is corrected to use proper SQL NULL instead of the string literal 'null', preventing both injection and unintended data corruption.
assumptions: The affected version range is inferred from the explicit context (affected_version '0', fixed_version '<=4.0.0'); the exact starting version is not confirmed by the patch itself.
PR:L assumes the attacker can write to the database via an authenticated application role or direct DB access; the specific authentication mechanism is not stated in the patch.
The CVSS impact ratings (VC:H, VI:H, VA:H) assume the database user has broad privileges; if the DB account is highly restricted, impact could be lower.
CAPEC-126 is selected as the closest match; the stored/timed nature of the injection (data planted before migration runs) is a variant not explicitly covered by a more specific CAPEC.
The patch does not indicate whether the migration has already been executed in deployed instances, which would affect real-world exploitability.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In migrations/versions/5cd03995339b_.py, four SQL statements (two SELECT and two UPDATE) are converted from Python f-string interpolation to SQLAlchemy parameterized queries using named bind parameters (:case_id, :instance_id, :ident, :id, :task_id). The NULL identifier handling is changed from assigning the string 'null' to assigning Python None, which SQLAlchemy translates to a proper SQL NULL value.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:L: The migration runs locally on the application server; exploitation requires local access to the database. AC:H: High complexity because the attacker must first write a crafted identifier into the database and then wait for a migration to execute. AT:P: Attack targeting is present; the attacker must specifically craft a malicious SQL payload in the identifier field. PR:L: Low privilege; the attacker needs write access to the database (e.g., an authenticated application user or DB access). UI:N: The migration runs automatically during upgrade; no user interaction is required at trigger time. VC:H, VI:H, VA:H: Successful SQL injection allows arbitrary read, write, and destructive operations on the database. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N: Impact is confined to the local database; no evidence of cross-component or cross-system impact.

capecRationale.rationale: The vulnerability is a textbook SQL injection: attacker-controlled data (stored connector identifiers) is concatenated into SQL statements without sanitization or parameterization. CAPEC-126 is the most direct and specific match. The stored nature of the injection (data planted earlier, executed later during migration) is a variant but still falls squarely within this pattern.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The patch directly replaces f-string interpolation of stored values into SQL with parameterized queries, which is the canonical fix for CWE-89. The commit message explicitly states that stored identifiers were 'interpolated into SQL, allowing expressions to execute,' confirming SQL injection.

solutions.value: The vulnerability is remediated by replacing direct string interpolation of stored database values into SQL queries with parameterized (bound) queries, ensuring that user-supplied or stored data is treated strictly as data rather than executable SQL. descriptions.value:
A SQL injection vulnerability exists in a database migration script in flowintel.

The migration process reads stored connector identifier values from the database and interpolates them directly into SQL statements without parameterization. An attacker who has previously written a malicious identifier value into the affected tables can cause arbitrary SQL execution when the migration is subsequently run during an application upgrade.

- Requires prior write access to the database to plant a malicious identifier value
- Triggered automatically during a migration or upgrade operation
- Can result in unauthorized data disclosure, modification, or deletion

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.0.0

references.name: Streaming request body limit enforced only after an 8 MB read in elixir-grpc grpc_server

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming requests.

The streaming read clause of GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.Handler.info/3 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy/handler.ex) asks Cowboy for up to 8,000,000 bytes per read and compares the running total with max_body_size only after the read returns. The gRPC length prefix of a message is not checked before the message is buffered. Each stream can therefore buffer up to one full read beyond the configured limit before it is refused, and many concurrent streams exhaust node memory. Releases before 1.0.6 apply no limit to streaming requests at all.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Large reads

async_read_body/2 asks Cowboy for up to 8,000,000 bytes per read on the streaming path, whatever max_body_size is set to.

2. The limit is checked after the read

track_body_bytes/2 adds each returned chunk to a running total and refuses the stream with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED only once the total exceeds max_body_size. By then the whole chunk is in memory.

3. No check on the length prefix

The 5-byte gRPC prefix can declare up to 4 GiB. The server does not compare it with any limit before buffering, so a prefix that declares an oversized message does not stop the read.

4. Result

Each client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming call can make the server hold several megabytes more than the configured limit, and the attacker can open many such calls at once. Before 1.0.6 the streaming path had no limit, and GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.reading_stream/1 buffered the whole body.

cna.title: Apache Commons Codec: NUL bytes in tree entry names cause Git/SWHID identifier collisions (GitIdentifiers class)

descriptions.value:
The GitIdentifiers class in Apache Commons Codec did not reject NUL bytes in tree entry names. Because Git uses a NUL byte to mark the end of each entry name in a tree object, a crafted name could make one tree serialize to the same bytes as a different tree. Two different directory trees could then receive the same Git tree identifier or SWHID.



The impact is limited: common file systems do not allow NUL bytes in file names, so trees built by walking a file system are not affected. Only applications that build trees from names supplied by other sources, such as entries of archive formats that permit NUL bytes in names (e.g. ZIP) or names passed directly to the API, are exposed.



This issue affects Apache Commons Codec: from 1.22.0 before 1.23.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: IBM1390/IBM1399 encoders may read past input

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes to check the next UCS-4 code point.  The check for end of buffer however does not account for this, which may result in a buffer overread if the following code point has less than 4 bytes remaining.  Exploitation of this bug not only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but also strict control over layout of the input in memory.

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag.

With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth.

A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.

cna.title: JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing colon in decode_hv

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing colon in decode_hv.

Unless it is short plain ASCII, a quoted key is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in BusyBox. The udhcpc6 DHCPv6 client does not properly validate the size of network options sent by a server before copying them into memory. A malicious DHCPv6 server on the local network can exploit this flaw by sending a crafted reply, triggering a stack-based buffer overflow. cna.title: Integer underflow of the record data length in IODWrite requests

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user record index against the size of the record block header. The 32-bit length is reduced by the header size before it is passed to the record handlers, so a length smaller than the header underflows and the handlers receive a data length of about 65530. The fixed-size reads of the I&M and PDPort handlers can then read past the end of the session buffer. The result of the write is discarded. The attacker must have an established Application Relationship or be able to send in the context of one, and requires ADJACENT network access.
