cna.title: ip6: vti: Use ip6_tnl.net in vti6_changelink().

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The bug is reached only through rtnetlink configuration (RTM_NEWLINK changelink and RTM_SETLINK netns move via `ip link`), not through remote packet handling on the vti6 tunnel itself.
AC:L - Exploitation is a deterministic, attacker-controlled sequence (create vti6, move netns, changelink, delete netns) with no races or external victim state required.
PR:L - The fix commit and rtnetlink path confirm reachability with CAP_NET_ADMIN inside an unprivileged user+network namespace (`unshare --user --map-root-user --net`), not init-namespace root.
UI:N - No victim interaction is required; the attacker triggers the bug entirely through their own netlink operations.
S:C - On container hosts, an unprivileged tenant can corrupt namespace teardown and panic the host kernel, impacting resources outside the attacker's security scope (other tenants and the host).
C:H - The stale per-netns hash leaves `cleanup_net()`/`vti6_exit_rtnl_net()` walking freed `ip6_tnl` list nodes, constituting a use-after-free with arbitrary kernel memory read potential.
I:H - Cross-netns hash corruption can leave dangling pointers and drive `unregister_netdevice_queue()` on already-freed devices (kernel BUG at net/core/dev.c:12376), enabling memory corruption exploitable for control-flow hijacking.
A:H - The published reproducer reliably triggers a kernel BUG during namespace cleanup, causing host-wide denial of service via kernel panic/oops.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ip6: vti: Use ip6_tnl.net in vti6_changelink().

ip netns add ns1
ip netns add ns2
ip -n ns1 link add vti6_test type vti6 remote ::1 local ::2 key 7
ip -n ns1 link set vti6_test netns ns2
ip -n ns2 link set vti6_test type vti6 remote ::3 local ::4 key 9
ip netns del ns2
ip netns del ns1
[  132.495484] ------------[ cut here ]------------
[  132.497609] kernel BUG at net/core/dev.c:12376!

Commit 61220ab34948 ("vti6: Enable namespace changing") dropped
NETIF_F_NETNS_LOCAL from vti6 devices. A vti6 tunnel can then
move through IFLA_NET_NS_FD. After the move dev_net(dev) points
at the new netns while t->net stays at the creation netns.

vti6_changelink() and vti6_update() still use dev_net(dev) and
dev_net(t->dev). They unlink from one per netns hash and relink
into another. The creation netns is left with a stale entry.
cleanup_net() of that netns later walks freed memory.

Reachable from an unprivileged user namespace (unshare --user
--map-root-user --net). Cross tenant scope on container hosts.

cna.title: wifi: mt76: add wcid publish check in mt76_sta_add

scenarios.value:
AV:A - The bug is reached through WiFi RX/TX-status DMA processing and station add during 802.11 association/roaming, both triggered by frames from a peer on the same wireless segment. Per kernel WiFi guidance, frame-driven driver bugs are Adjacent, not Network.
AC:L - An adjacent attacker can reliably create the race by sending deauth/association traffic to force sta re-add while flooding data frames to keep the RX poll path active; both sides of the race are attacker-influenced and repeatable.
PR:N - Exploitation requires no Linux privileges—only the ability to send 802.11 management/data frames as a nearby WiFi peer (rogue AP, deauth attacker, or associating client on AP mode), with no authentication to the victim host.
UI:N - No victim user action is required beyond normal WiFi operation; deauth-forced roaming and automatic reassociation drive the vulnerable sta_add path without user interaction.
S:U - Impact is kernel heap/list corruption within the same security authority; this is not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-namespace boundary violation.
C:H - Reinitializing an embedded list_head while still linked corrupts kernel linked-list metadata in kmalloc-backed structures; list corruption is memory corruption that can be leveraged for arbitrary kernel memory disclosure.
I:H - The corrupted doubly-linked list enables list-poisoning style arbitrary kernel writes and potential control-flow hijacking, not merely a bounded or transient modification.
A:H - The reproducer triggers kernel list_add corruption detection and crash; corrupted sta_poll_list integrity can cause kernel panic/oops during normal WiFi operation.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mt76: add wcid publish check in mt76_sta_add

Since mt7925_mac_sta_add publishes wcid, add publish check in mt76_sta_add
to avoid reinitializing the wcid->poll_list.

Found dev->sta_poll_list corruption when using mt7925 and 7.1-rc4.
According to the corruption information, prev->next was changed to itself.

wlan0: disconnect from AP 90:fb:5d:94:8b:e3 for new auth to 90:fb:5d:94:8b:e2
wlan0: authenticate with 90:fb:5d:94:8b:e2 (local address=84:9e:56:9c:7e:6b)
wlan0: send auth to 90:fb:5d:94:8b:e2 (try 1/3)
 slab kmalloc-8k start ffff8c80958a6000 pointer offset 4160 size 8192
list_add corruption. prev->next should be next (ffff8c808a7488f8), but was ffff8c80958a7040. (prev=ffff8c80958a7040).

 mt76_wcid_add_poll+0x95/0xd0 [mt76]
 mt7925_mac_add_txs.part.0+0xa5/0xe0 [mt7925_common]
 mt7925_rx_check+0xa7/0xc0 [mt7925_common]
 mt76_dma_rx_poll+0x50d/0x790 [mt76]
 mt792x_poll_rx+0x52/0xe0 [mt792x_lib]

cna.title: Apache HTTP Server: mod_vhost_alias stack overflow

descriptions.value:
Stack-based buffer overflow in mod_vhost_alias in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server through 2.4.68 on all platforms allows a remote client to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code via an HTTP request with a Host header exceeding 8192 bytes when VirtualDocumentRoot uses a hostname format specifier and LimitRequestFieldSize is raised above the default.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.4.69, which fixes this issue.

Stack-based buffer overflow in mod_vhost_alias in Apache Software Foundation Apache HTTP Server through 2.4.68 on all platforms allows a remote client to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code via an HTTP request with a Host header exceeding 8192 bytes when VirtualDocumentRoot uses a hostname format specifier and LimitRequestFieldSize is raised above the default.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.4.69, which fixes this issue.

cna.title: Mongoose: ppp_handle_ipv6cp() uses attacker-controlled length without bounds check — OOB read and heap overflow (PPP/PPPoE, MG_ENABLE_IPV6)

descriptions.value: Mongoose is an embedded web server and network library. Prior to 7.23, ppp_handle_ipv6cp() in src/l2_ppp.c trusts the 16-bit IPv6CP len field without checking it against the received payload size. On a PPP or PPPoE link using MG_ENABLE_TCPIP and MG_ENABLE_IPV6, an unauthenticated adjacent peer can complete the required LCP exchange and send a short Configure-Request with an oversized length, causing ppp_tx_frame() to read beyond recv_queue.buf and write beyond tx.buf. The same length misuse can also expose adjacent heap bytes in a reply or hang the event loop through find_opt(). This issue is fixed in version 7.23.

cna.title: drm/gem: fix race between change_handle and handle_delete

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Exploitation requires local ioctl calls on /dev/dri/renderD* or /dev/dri/card* through DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CHANGE_HANDLE and DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE; there is no network-facing path to this code.
AC:L - The attacker controls both racing threads from the same process (one issuing GEM_CHANGE_HANDLE, one issuing GEM_CLOSE on the old handle) and can repeat until the window is hit; this is a self-induced race, not one dependent on external timing.
PR:L - Only DRM_RENDER_ALLOW is required, available to unprivileged local users with access to a render node (common on desktops, Android, browsers' GPU processes, and cloud GPU instances); no CAP_SYS_ADMIN or init-namespace root is needed.
UI:N - No victim interaction is required beyond the attacker already having render-node access; the race is triggered entirely by the attacker's own concurrent ioctl calls.
S:C - Successful exploitation crosses from a sandboxed application security boundary (browser GPU process, Android app sandbox, or container with passed-through GPU device) into kernel memory, enabling privilege escalation beyond the attacker's original security scope.
C:H - The bug is a GEM object use-after-free; freed kernel heap objects can be reallocated and dereferenced via subsequent GEM operations, enabling arbitrary kernel memory disclosure.
I:H - Use-after-free of a drm_gem_object allows heap grooming and corruption of reallocated objects, providing a standard path to arbitrary kernel write and local privilege escalation/code execution.
A:H - The race can free a GEM object still referenced by ioctl state, causing kernel oops/panic on dereference of freed memory; UAF bugs also carry inherent crash risk even before full exploitation.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/gem: fix race between change_handle and handle_delete

drm_gem_change_handle_ioctl leaves the old handle live in the IDR
during the window between spin_unlock(table_lock) and the final
spin_lock(table_lock). A concurrent drm_gem_handle_delete on the old
handle succeeds in this window, decrements handle_count to 0, and frees
the GEM object while the new handle's IDR entry still references it.

NULL the old handle's IDR entry before dropping table_lock so that any
concurrent GEM_CLOSE on the old handle sees NULL and returns -EINVAL.
Restore the old entry on the prime-bookkeeping error path.

cna.title: Omnispace Agora Project < 26.10.0 SQL Injection via sortEvents Parameter

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Omnispace Agora Project < 26.10.0 SQL Injection via sortEvents Parameter

descriptions.value: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.10.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the calendar functionality that allows attackers to inject malicious SQL by manipulating the sortEvents parameter, which is concatenated into the ORDER BY clause without sanitization in app/ModCalendar/CtrlCalendar.php. Attackers can exploit this flaw using error-based techniques such as extractvalue payloads to extract database information, including version data, from the underlying system.

cna.title: mptcp: close TOCTOU race while computing rcv_wnd

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The flaw is in the MPTCP TCP output path (`__tcp_transmit_skb()` → `mptcp_established_options_dss()` / `mptcp_write_options()`), reachable by any remote peer that can exchange MPTCP packets over the network.
AC:L - The attacker controls both sides of the race by timing concurrent ingress traffic (advancing `msk->ack_seq` on receive) against egress transmissions on the same or another subflow; no special memory layout or victim-specific state is required.
PR:N - Exploitation requires only the ability to complete an MPTCP/TCP connection as a remote peer; no local privileges, capabilities, or authenticated access to the victim system is needed.
UI:N - Exploitation is fully automated over the network once an MPTCP connection is established; no victim user action is required beyond normal service connectivity.
S:U - The impact is confined to the kernel networking stack and the affected MPTCP connection state; it does not cross a VM, sandbox, or IOMMU security boundary.
C:N - This is a protocol-state TOCTOU inconsistency, not a memory-safety bug; it does not provide arbitrary or bounded kernel memory disclosure.
I:L - Inconsistent DSS ACK versus receive-window tracking can corrupt MPTCP-level window state (`rcv_wnd_sent`), allowing acceptance or handling of data outside the window actually announced to the peer.
A:H - A remote attacker can repeatedly trigger the race to cause connection disruption (reset/fallback), stall MPTCP sessions, and inflate out-of-order receive buffering via incorrect `rcv_wnd_sent` values, denying service to applications using the connection.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: close TOCTOU race while computing rcv_wnd

The MPTCP output path access locklessly the MPTCP-level ack_seq
in multiple times, using possibly different values for the data_ack
in the DSS option and to compute the announced rcv wnd for the same
packet.

Refactor the cote to avoid inconsistencies which may confuse the
peer. Also ensure that the MPTCP level rcv wnd is updated only when
the egress packet actually contains a DSS ack.

cna.title: SurrealDB before 3.2.0 SSRF via JWKS URL hostname resolution

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: SurrealDB before 3.2.0 SSRF via JWKS URL hostname resolution

descriptions.value: SurrealDB before 3.2.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the JWKS fetcher that validates only the URL hostname string against allow-lists without checking resolved IP addresses. An Owner role attacker can point an access method at an allow-listed hostname resolving to private or loopback addresses, causing the server to issue GET requests to internal addresses that would be blocked by direct URL.

cna.title: Bluetooth: HIDP: fix missing length checks in hidp_input_report()

scenarios.value:
AV:A - The bug is reached when a connected Bluetooth HID peer sends malformed HIDP interrupt (or control DATA) frames over L2CAP ACL; packets traverse HCI → l2cap_recv_acldata() → l2cap_data_channel() → l2cap_sock_recv_cb() → HIDP session thread → hidp_recv_intr_frame()/hidp_process_data() → hidp_input_report(), which is an adjacent Bluetooth attack surface.
AC:L - Exploitation only requires sending deliberately truncated HIDP input reports on an already-established HIDP/L2CAP session; the attacker fully controls packet length and can trigger the out-of-bounds read reliably on every malformed frame with no race or special memory layout.
PR:N - The attacker is an external Bluetooth HID device sending L2CAP payloads and needs no Linux account, capability, or namespace privilege; CAP_NET_ADMIN is only required for bluetoothd to register the session, not for the malicious peer to deliver the crafted packets.
UI:N - Once a HIDP session is active, exploitation is automatic from crafted Bluetooth traffic and requires no further victim action; pairing/connection is an attacker prerequisite, not user interaction at exploit time (consistent with prior Bluetooth HIDP CNA scoring such as CVE-2026-23462).
S:U - Impact is confined to kernel HIDP/input handling and forged input events delivered within the same kernel security authority; it does not cross a VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary.
C:H - The vulnerable code performs out-of-bounds reads of up to eight keyboard or four mouse payload bytes beyond skb->len, and per CVSS kernel guidance any out-of-bounds read is rated High because adjacent skb tailroom may contain stale packet or kernel heap data observable through phantom key/mouse event side channels.
I:H - Out-of-bounds bytes are interpreted as boot-protocol keyboard scancodes and mouse button/movement events, enabling phantom key presses and pointer injection into the system input layer; on laptops, kiosks, automotive consoles, and Android handsets this can forge arbitrary keystrokes/clicks against the active user session.
A:H - Reading keyboard/mouse payload bytes past valid skb->len is undefined behavior on tightly allocated skbs with no tailroom and can fault the kernel; even when reads stay within tailroom, forged input can repeatedly disrupt session availability on shared/public Bluetooth keyboard deployments, and under the conservative scoring rule this is rated High when crash potential cannot be excluded.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: HIDP: fix missing length checks in hidp_input_report()

hidp_input_report() reads keyboard and mouse payload data from an skb
without first verifying that skb->len contains enough data.

hidp_recv_intr_frame() pulls the 1-byte HIDP header before dispatching
to hidp_input_report(). If a paired device sends a truncated packet,
the handler reads beyond the valid skb data, resulting in an
out-of-bounds read of skb data. The OOB bytes may be interpreted as
phantom key presses or spurious mouse movement.

Replace the open-coded length tracking and pointer arithmetic with
skb_pull_data() calls. skb_pull_data() returns NULL if the requested
bytes are not present, eliminating the need for a manual size variable
and the separate skb->len guard.

cna.title: Zammad: Sensitive Information Exposure in Integration Administration API

descriptions.value: Zammad is a web based open source helpdesk/customer support system. In 7.0.3 and 7.1.1, an authenticated administrator can obtain stored integration credentials in cleartext through the integration administration API. Certain responses do not consistently mask sensitive fields, so configured secrets can be returned in plain text instead of the expected masked placeholder. Both the LDAP and Exchange integrations are affected. This issue is fixed in version 7.1.2.

cna.title: draw.io: Path traversal in ExportProxyServlet allows access to arbitrary backend endpoints

descriptions.value: draw.io is a configurable diagramming and whiteboarding application. Prior to version 30.2.7, src/main/java/com/mxgraph/online/ExportProxyServlet.java uses request.getPathInfo() to build a proxyPath and appends it directly to EXPORT_URL without rejecting dot segments or confirming that the normalized destination remains under the configured export path. An unauthenticated request containing traversal segments can therefore address unintended routes on the internal export server, and the servlet forwards all request headers and the request body to that destination, allowing arbitrary header injection. Depending on the export service configuration, exploitation can expose administration, debugging, health, or configuration endpoints and can permit unintended internal actions. This issue is fixed in version 30.2.7.

descriptions.description: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

descriptions.value: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious HTML markup by controlling imported directory data or an uploaded CSV file, as values are rendered into table cell text and value attributes after only Txt::utf8Encode() with no HTML escaping in VuePersonsImportExport.php. Attackers can craft a CSV cell containing an attribute-breakout payload that is rendered verbatim and executed in the browser of the administrator performing the import, leading to arbitrary script execution in the administrative context.

cna.title: ip6: vti: Use ip6_tnl.net in vti6_siocdevprivate().

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Exploitation requires a local ioctl(SIOCCHGTUNNEL) on a migrated vti6 netdev via socket/dev_ioctl; the bug is in vti6_siocdevprivate(), not in remote packet reception.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls namespace creation, tunnel migration (IFLA_NET_NS_FD), and ioctl parameters to collide with a victim tunnel; the commit documents a deterministic, reproducible sequence with no uncontrollable race.
PR:L - Only CAP_NET_ADMIN in the migrated (attacker) network namespace is required, obtainable via unprivileged user namespaces (unshare --user --map-root-user --net); the missing check against the creation namespace's user_ns is the core flaw.
UI:N - No victim interaction is needed; the attacker performs all setup steps (create/migrate tunnel, issue SIOCCHGTUNNEL) autonomously.
S:C - The attack hijacks IPsec/XFRM traffic destined for tunnels in a different tenant's network namespace on container hosts, crossing container/tenant security boundaries rather than staying within the attacker's own scope.
C:H - After hash poisoning, xfrm receive delivers matched/decapsulated packets to the attacker-controlled netdev, enabling interception of victim VPN/IPsec traffic including potentially sensitive plaintext after decryption.
I:H - The attacker gains control over which netdev receives victim tunnel traffic and can read, drop, or forward/modify decapsulated packets, constituting unauthorized manipulation of another tenant's network data path.
A:H - Hijacking the creation-namespace hash bucket causes the legitimate victim tunnel to stop receiving matched traffic, producing denial of service to the victim's IPsec connectivity.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ip6: vti: Use ip6_tnl.net in vti6_siocdevprivate().

After patch 1/2 in this series, vti6_update() unlinks and relinks
the tunnel through t->net. vti6_siocdevprivate() still uses
dev_net(dev) for the collision lookup. For a tunnel moved through
IFLA_NET_NS_FD, dev_net(dev) is the new netns, not t->net.

SIOCCHGTUNNEL on a migrated tunnel then runs:

  net = dev_net(dev)                    /* migrated netns */
  t   = vti6_locate(net, &p1, false)    /* misses target in t->net */
  ...
  t   = netdev_priv(dev)
  vti6_update(t, &p1, false)            /* mutates t->net's hash */

A caller in the migrated netns picks params that match a tunnel
in the creation netns. The lookup in dev_net(dev) finds nothing.
vti6_update() prepends the migrated tunnel at the head of the
creation netns hash bucket for those params. Later lookups in
the creation netns resolve to the migrated device. xfrm receive
delivers the matched packets through a device the caller controls.

Reachable from an unprivileged user namespace (unshare --user
--map-root-user --net). Cross tenant scope on container hosts.

Switch the SIOCCHGTUNNEL path on a non fallback device to use
t->net for the lookup. The lookup now matches the netns
vti6_update() operates on.

Also add ns_capable(self->net->user_ns, CAP_NET_ADMIN) before
the lookup. The check at the top of the case is against
dev_net(dev)->user_ns, which after migration is the attacker's
netns. A caller there can pick params absent from self->net,
the lookup returns NULL, t becomes self, and vti6_update()
inserts the device into the creation netns hash. The new check
requires CAP_NET_ADMIN in the creation netns user_ns too.

SIOCADDTUNNEL and SIOCCHGTUNNEL on the fallback device keep
dev_net(dev), which equals init_net there.

Prior to 2.2.0, OmniAuth derives provider callback URLs from request-controlled host information when neither a fixed full_host nor framework-level incoming host validation is configured. A remote unauthenticated client can supply a forged Host header, creating a host header injection risk in applications whose web framework does not verify incoming host headers. Applications using appropriately configured Rails host authorization or a fixed full_host are not affected by this path. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.0.

cna.title: Unleash: Unauthenticated single-request DoS via OpenAPI validation error formatter

descriptions.value: Unleash is an open-source feature management platform. Prior to 7.5.2, 7.6.5, and 8.0.2, the shared OpenAPI validation error path in src/lib/error/bad-data-error.ts passes a raw request value from lodash.get to JSON.stringify in genericErrorMessage and fromOpenApiValidationErrors without guarding stack exhaustion. An unauthenticated attacker can send a roughly 10 KB JSON value nested thousands of levels deep to POST /edge/validate, POST /edge/issue-token, or another OpenAPI-validated endpoint, causing RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded in openAPIValidationMiddleware and terminating the Node process because no uncaughtException handler recovers it. Replaying the request can sustain a complete service outage. This issue is fixed in versions 7.5.2, 7.6.5, and 8.0.2.

cna.title: Incorrect Authorization in Kibana Leading to Machine Learning Audit Log Integrity Compromise

descriptions.value: CAPEC-1 Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs

Incorrect Authorization (CWE-863) in Kibana can lead to integrity compromise of Machine Learning audit and notification records via Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs (CAPEC-1).

A vulnerability exists in Kibana's Machine Learning functionality where a Machine Learning management endpoint performs an insufficient authorization check. The endpoint validates only a coarse privilege level but does not verify that the requesting user has access to the specific Machine Learning job or notification resources provided in the request. As a result, a low-privileged user with Machine Learning access in any Kibana space can manipulate Machine Learning audit and notification records for arbitrary jobs—including jobs in other spaces or belonging to other users—by leveraging Kibana's internally elevated credentials to write to restricted Machine Learning system indices that the user cannot access directly.

cna.title: OpenRemote has authenticated SQL injection in crosstab datapoint exports

descriptions.value: OpenRemote is an open-source internet-of-things platform. Prior to 1.26.0, the `datapoint export` API constructs `CSV crosstab` SQL by concatenating an `asset name` and `attribute name` into a `COPY` query that uses `crosstab` and streams `TO STDOUT`. The `asset name` enters both a double-quoted column identifier and a category query enclosed by the fixed `$cat$` delimiter. Escaping single quotes in one string context does not escape embedded double quotes in identifiers or protect that dollar-quote boundary. An authenticated user permitted to create or rename an asset and read/export datapoints for one of its attributes can store SQL metacharacters in the name and request a `crosstab` export, causing injected SELECT output to be returned in the normal ZIP/CSV response. This enables database exfiltration without direct database or filesystem access or token forgery. In a multi-tenant deployment it can expose other tenants' data if the manager's database role can read shared tables; integrity and availability effects are not established by the demonstrated read primitive. This issue is fixed in version 1.26.0.

descriptions.value: The SMS control function of IE-SR-2TX-WL-4G devices can require a password for SMS commands via the 'Enable Password Authorization' setting. cna.title: BentoPDF: Workflow Import Allows Unvalidated TSA URL Leading to PDF Hash Exfiltration via RFC 3161 Requests

descriptions.description: CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

descriptions.value: BentoPDF is a client-side PDF toolkit that is self hostable. In 2.8.6 and earlier, deserializeWorkflow() accepts the Timestamp node's tsaUrl control from imported JSON without schema or destination validation. When a user imports the crafted workflow and runs it against a PDF, timestampPdf() sends an RFC 3161 TimeStampReq containing the PDF's SHA-256 MessageImprint to the attacker-selected endpoint. The default self-hosted configuration does not set VITE_CORS_PROXY_URL, so the request bypasses the proxy's ALLOWED_TSA_HOSTS checks and is sent directly. The disclosed digest can confirm that a document matches a known file and can correlate the same document across users without revealing its contents. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.8.7.

cna.title: TAKO AI Agent for Okta: Unauthenticated first-run administrator takeover

descriptions.value: TAKO AI Agent for Okta is a local-first AI agent that helps Okta administrators query tenant data using natural language. Prior to 3.0.1-beta, `POST /api/auth/setup` in `src/api/routers/auth.py` allows an unauthenticated network attacker to create the first administrator account before the legitimate owner completes initial setup. The `initial_setup` function checks only the `is_setup` completion flag and requires no authentication, one-time bootstrap token, or network restriction. The default `docker-compose.yml` publishes port 8001 on all interfaces, the `Dockerfile` starts the listener on 0.0.0.0, and `src/api/main.py` mounts the authentication router without a global authentication guard. The endpoint invokes `create_auth_user` with `UserRole.ADMIN` and `set_auth_cookie`, issuing a valid `fctr_session` JWT cookie. Localhost-only CORS rules do not restrict non-browser HTTP clients, and the setup operation does not require access to a real Okta tenant. The attacker becomes the sole administrator and prevents legitimate first-run setup, can read Okta-synced user data, API tokens, chat history, and application configuration, modify users and Okta integration credentials, and lock out administrators or disable the service. Already completed setup is rejected. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.1-beta.

cna.title: Glance 0.8.5 IP Spoofing Authentication Brute-Force Protection Bypass

descriptions.value: Glance through 0.8.5 contains an IP address spoofing vulnerability in the authentication handler that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass brute-force lockout protections by supplying arbitrary values in the X-Forwarded-For request header when the server proxied option is enabled. Attackers can manipulate the leftmost value of the X-Forwarded-For header to make each login attempt appear to originate from a distinct IP address, preventing the per-IP failed-login counter from reaching the lockout threshold and enabling unlimited credential guessing against the authentication endpoint.

cna.title: pgjdbc simple query mode quotes parameters for the wrong standard_conforming_strings value

descriptions.value: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, can quote a string parameter for the wrong value of standard_conforming_strings when preferQueryMode=simple is set. A statement, trigger or configuration reload can turn the setting off during a session. A parameter value with a backslash and a quote then ends the literal, and the rest of the value runs as SQL. Before 42.7.6 any session with the setting off was affected. The statement cache can also reuse a parse made under the other setting. With allowEncodingChanges=true and the EUC_JP or SJIS client encoding, the yen sign acts as a backslash. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

descriptions.description: CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

solutions.value: Upgrade to pgjdbc 42.7.15 or later.

workarounds.value: Use the default extended query mode, or keep standard_conforming_strings on.

cna.title: Krita ASL File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

descriptions.value:
Krita ASL File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of ASL files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28906.

descriptions.value: pypdf before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to cause large memory usage by supplying crafted PDF cross-reference streams. Attackers can craft a PDF whose cross-reference stream offsets all point to one large object, exhausting memory in applications parsing the file.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: pypdf before 7.0.0 Memory Exhaustion via Cross-Reference Streams with Identical Offsets

cna.title: pgjdbc leaves a half-written message on the connection after an unchecked exception

descriptions.value: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not close the connection when an unchecked exception interrupts a request. Part of a Bind message stays in the send buffer, and the server reads the bytes that follow as the rest of it. The bytes of a value uploaded later on the same connection can then run as a SQL command. Since 42.6.0 a setBinaryStream() value without a length that is executed again throws such an exception, as does the driver's own retry after SQLState 0A000 or 26000. An application stream that throws an unchecked exception has the same effect in all versions. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

descriptions.description: CWE-755 Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

solutions.value: Upgrade to pgjdbc 42.7.15 or later.

cna.title: Better Auth before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 Session Mix-Up via MySQL Serial IDs

descriptions.value: Better Auth (better-auth, @better-auth/kysely-adapter, and @better-auth/drizzle-adapter) before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition with MySQL or MariaDB serial IDs because the inserted row's ID is read via a separate LAST_INSERT_ID() query that may run on a different pooled connection. Under concurrent load, a user signing in can receive another user's session and act as that user.

descriptions.description: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Better Auth before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 Session Mix-Up via MySQL Serial IDs

cna.title: graphql-core 3.2.12 before 3.2.14 and 3.3.0rc1 before 3.3.2 Denial of Service via Parser max_tokens Comment Runs

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: graphql-core 3.2.12 before 3.2.14 and 3.3.0rc1 before 3.3.2 Denial of Service via Parser max_tokens Comment Runs

descriptions.value: graphql-core 3.2.12 before 3.2.14 and 3.3.0rc1 before 3.3.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the parser max_tokens limit using long runs of comments. Attackers can submit GraphQL documents of consecutive comments that Lexer.lookahead fully tokenizes before limit checks, consuming CPU and memory proportional to document size.

descriptions.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

cna.title: Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.98 Link Following via .actrc --eventpath

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.98 Link Following via .actrc --eventpath

Attackers can commit an event.json symlink pointing to files like ~/.ssh/id_rsa, which act copies into the job container as GITHUB_EVENT_PATH for workflow steps to exfiltrate.

descriptions.description: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

cna.title: better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 Unverified Phone Number Account Takeover

descriptions.value: better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in the phone number plugin that lets sign-up and other flows save unverified phone numbers, which phone OTP sign-in then uses to select the account. Attackers can attach a victim's number to an attacker-controlled account so the victim's valid OTP sign-in yields a session for that account, exposing data the victim then enters.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 Unverified Phone Number Account Takeover

Attackers controlling a lookalike mailbox using a dotless i or other case-folding variant receive the victim's reset link, since it is sent to the typed address, and set a new password.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 Path Traversal to Stored XSS via File Rename

descriptions.value: N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) before 20261121.1943 does not restrict the destination of the LDAP synchronisation connection check performed when a relay is configured. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose animation accessor describes more values than its float_array holds to read past the array or dereference null, crashing the importing application.

cna.title: Quay: quay: registry jwt accepted as robot password enables privilege elevation

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Quay. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker holding a restricted, short-lived JSON Web Token (JWT) to achieve privilege escalation. Because Quay improperly accepts scoped registry bearer tokens as valid robot account passwords, an attacker can authenticate directly as the robot account and obtain broader permissions. Consequently, unauthorized access persists and enables the attacker to generate fresh tokens even after the robot account's password has been reset.

cna.title: Cesanta Mongoose 7.22 before 7.24 Out-of-Bounds Read via mg_timegm

cna.title: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Path Traversal via Windows Backslashes in Bucket Keys

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 Path Traversal via Windows Backslashes in Bucket Keys

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Vikunja from 0.20.5 before 2.8.0 Login CSRF via OIDC Callback State Check

cna.title: Frappe ERPNext 4.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Module Taxes Endpoint

cna.title: Umami 3.3.0 before 3.5.0 2FA Bypass via Race Condition in /api/2fa/verify

cna.title: @better-auth/electron before 1.7.16 Auth Secret Disclosure and Two-Factor Bypass

descriptions.value: @better-auth/electron 1.5.0-beta.12 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 accepts any validly signed value as its transfer cookie and returns the full endpoint context, including the auth secret and social provider client secrets, in sign-in responses. cna.title: Web-Token jwt-framework before 3.4.10 DoS via Unbounded PBES2 p2c Iteration Count

cna.title: pgjdbc GSS encryption accepts replayed packets and can stop encrypting

descriptions.value: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not check the token state that GSSContext.unwrap() reports on a GSS-encrypted connection. An attacker on the network path can replay an earlier server packet from the same connection, and the driver accepts it as the answer to the current query. The driver also shares one MessageProp between reading and writing. One integrity-only packet from the server then makes the driver send later SQL and parameters without encryption. Only connections with gssEncMode=prefer or require that start GSS encryption are affected. Versions 42.2.15 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

descriptions.description: CWE-319 Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

solutions.value: Upgrade to pgjdbc 42.7.15 or later.

workarounds.value: Set gssEncMode=disable and use TLS for transport encryption instead.

cna.title: pgjdbc stores a different number for a BigDecimal outside the binary numeric range

descriptions.value: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, cuts the weight and scale of a BigDecimal to 16 bits when it sends the value in binary, which is the default. The server then stores a different number without an error. For example 999999.99e-262144 is stored as 999999.99, so a tiny value can pass a range check and be stored as a large one. The driver also computes 10 to the power of the scale first, so a short value such as 1e-200000000 keeps a thread busy for minutes. Versions 42.3.0 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

solutions.value: Upgrade to pgjdbc 42.7.15 or later.

workarounds.value: Set binaryTransfer=false, or reject BigDecimal values with a very large or very small exponent before binding them.

cna.title: pgjdbc lets a NUL character in a connection property add startup parameters

On a server that trusts the client, the attacker can log in as any role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

descriptions.description: CWE-158 Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character

solutions.value: Upgrade to pgjdbc 42.7.15 or later.

workarounds.value: Refuse a NUL character in connection values that come from untrusted input.

cna.title: pgjdbc catalog queries can run objects of other database roles

descriptions.value: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, uses unqualified operators and functions in the catalog queries of DatabaseMetaData, ResultSetMetaData and TypeInfoCache. A role with CREATE on a schema of the application's search_path can add an operator with an exact type match, and the server runs it with the privileges of the application's role. TypeInfoCache also resolves an unqualified type name such as interval by its own ranking. A domain with that name in another schema, even the temporary schema of another session, can be used instead, and its CHECK runs in the application's session. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

cna.title: Krita TIF File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

descriptions.value:
Krita TIF File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of TIF files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28517.

cna.title: pgjdbc does not enforce TLS for some ssl, service and DataSource settings

descriptions.value: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not enforce TLS for some settings that ask for it. When sslmode is not set, an ssl value such as 1, on, yes or verify-full gives sslmode=prefer, or no TLS before 42.2.5. A service given in the Properties instead of the URL is ignored, so the sslmode of its pg_service.conf entry is lost. BaseDataSource.setUrl() keeps an sslmode, channelBinding or gssEncMode that was set before it. An attacker on the network path can then read and change the traffic. Versions 9.4.1208 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

descriptions.description: CWE-319 Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

solutions.value: Upgrade to pgjdbc 42.7.15 or later. From 42.7.15 an ssl value other than true, false or empty is refused.

workarounds.value: Set sslmode=verify-full in the URL or the Properties, and pass a service name in the URL.

descriptions.description: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

descriptions.value: odf-kit is a TypeScript and JavaScript library for working with OpenDocument Format files. An attacker can craft an ODS file that injects arbitrary HTML attributes or elements, allowing JavaScript execution in the host page's origin when an application inserts the converted output as HTML. Authenticated users with the Stock User role can send crafted reservation requests naming another order's item row to reserve stock beyond that order's limits, creating mismatched Stock Reservation Entries.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.122.0 Stock Reservation Validation Bypass

cna.title: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Taxes and Charges Templates

descriptions.value: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that allows authenticated users to read Taxes and Charges Template rows without permission checks. Attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read account heads and tax rates.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Taxes and Charges Templates

cna.title: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Type Confusion in gf_sg_command_apply MFNode Field Replace

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Type Confusion in gf_sg_command_apply MFNode Field Replace

descriptions.value: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that misinterprets single node values as child lists for MFNode field replace commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that causes an invalid node pointer to be dereferenced by gf_node_register(), crashing MP4Box for denial of service.

descriptions.description: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

descriptions.value: A weakness has been identified in twogood unshield up to 1.6.2. Impacted is the function unshield_get_cab_descriptor of the file lib/libunshield.c of the component Cabinet Descriptor Parser. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack requires local access. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

cna.title: Grav API Plugin 1.0.16 before 1.1.11 Scoped API Key Authorization Bypass

descriptions.value: Grav API plugin from 1.0.16 before 1.1.11 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows scoped API key holders to override page permission rules because checks read the owning account's authority instead of the key's scopes. Attackers can use keys minted on super-admin accounts to edit, delete or read pages that deny those actions, or use media-scoped keys to change media on read-only pages.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Grav API Plugin 1.0.16 before 1.1.11 Scoped API Key Authorization Bypass

cna.title: libexpat through 2.10.0 Isolated High Surrogate via UTF-16 Conversion

descriptions.value: libexpat through 2.10.0 contains an improper Unicode handling vulnerability in DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16 conversion functions in xmltok.c that can split valid surrogate pairs when output space is limited. In XML_UNICODE builds parsing non-native byte order UTF-16 input, attackers can supply crafted documents that deliver lone high surrogates to character data and default handlers.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: libexpat through 2.10.0 Isolated High Surrogate via UTF-16 Conversion

cna.title: mcp-server-kubernetes before 4.2.0 Argument Injection via Flag-Shaped Positional Operands

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: mcp-server-kubernetes before 4.2.0 Argument Injection via Flag-Shaped Positional Operands

descriptions.value: mcp-server-kubernetes before 4.2.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows remote MCP clients to inject kubectl flags by supplying dash-prefixed values as positional operands in tools such as exec_in_pod, kubectl_patch, and kubectl_logs. Attackers connected over SSE or Streamable HTTP transport can supply values like --filename to make kubectl read files from the server host, bypassing file-read restrictions.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

cna.title: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Item Records

descriptions.value: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns Item master records without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to retrieve complete item data including costing and purchase rates.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 Missing Authorization in Stock Module Item Records

cna.title: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in XMT Loader

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in XMT Loader

descriptions.value: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory when xmt_node_end() discards an out-of-scope node without resetting command-buffer state. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file that leaves parser->command_buffer and parser->command dangling, causing later parsing to access freed memory and crash MP4Box.

cna.title: VoidAuth before 1.19.2 ProxyAuth Access Control Bypass via Encoded Path Separators

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: VoidAuth before 1.19.2 ProxyAuth Access Control Bypass via Encoded Path Separators

descriptions.value: VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to evade stricter ProxyAuth domain rules by sending percent-encoded path separators. Attackers can request paths with encoded slashes, backslashes, semicolons, or dot segments that match a broader rule, reaching restricted paths once the reverse proxy or backend decodes them.

cna.title: OpenShot Video Editor through 4.1.1 Deserialization via Legacy Project Import

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenShot Video Editor through 4.1.1 Deserialization via Legacy Project Import

descriptions.value: OpenShot Video Editor (openshot-qt) through 4.1.1 contains an unsafe deserialization vulnerability in ProjectDataStore.load() and read_legacy_project_file() that passes non-JSON project files to pickle.load() without restriction. Attackers can trick users into opening a crafted .osp project file containing a pickle __reduce__ gadget to execute code with the user's privileges.

cna.title: FreeRDP before 3.33.1 Use-After-Free via WinPR LinkedList Enumerator

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FreeRDP before 3.33.1 Use-After-Free via WinPR LinkedList Enumerator

descriptions.value: FreeRDP before 3.33.1 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the WinPR wLinkedList collection because LinkedList_FreeNode() frees nodes without updating the cached list->current enumerator pointer. When calling code removes the node the enumerator references, LinkedList_Enumerator_MoveNext() or LinkedList_Enumerator_Current() reads freed heap memory, which can crash the process.

cna.title: ERPNext 14.44.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Payment Unreconciliation

descriptions.value: Frappe ERPNext 14.44.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Accounts module's payment unreconciliation endpoint, which does not check the caller's permission on the vouchers it unreconciles. Authenticated users with the Accounts User role can send crafted Unreconcile Payment requests naming vouchers from other companies or outside their User Permissions to remove their reconciliation.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: ERPNext 14.44.0 before 15.122.0 Missing Authorization in Accounts Payment Unreconciliation

cna.title: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 Schema Information Disclosure via Per-Type ACL Bypass

descriptions.value: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read schema definitions of denied types through listings ignoring per-type ACLs. Attackers can query the PostgreSQL wire catalog, GraphQL introspection, or MCP get_schema to reveal property names, indexes, inheritance, and materialized view SQL.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 Schema Information Disclosure via Per-Type ACL Bypass

cna.title: Coder 2.38.0 before 2.38.5 Symlink Path Traversal via read_skill_file

descriptions.value: Coder 2.32.0 before 2.34.17, 2.35.0 before 2.36.12, 2.37.0 before 2.37.9, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.5 contain a symlink-following flaw in the Coder Agents read_skill_file tool, which validates skill file paths lexically but follows symlinks outside the skill directory. Attackers who place a malicious skill containing a symlinked supporting file in a victim's workspace can leak other workspace files into the model context and chat history when the victim runs a chat using that skill.

cna.title: Krita PSB File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

descriptions.value:
Krita PSB File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of PSB files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28905.

source.value: Anonymous

cna.title: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Stack Buffer Overflow via xmt_resolve_od_links

Attackers can craft an XMT scene file whose URL fragment overflows the fixed 5000-byte szURL buffer via sprintf, crashing MP4Box when a user loads it.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 Stack Buffer Overflow via xmt_resolve_od_links

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Channel-variable injection via SIP REFER leads to command execution in mod_sofia

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, sofia_handle_sip_i_refer() placed raw Refer-To URI parameters and headers inside a sip_invite_params channel-variable block passed to switch_ivr_originate(). The originate parser treated a comma in the attacker-controlled value as a variable separator, allowing an authenticated caller on a bridged call to inject arbitrary variables into a newly originated leg. An injected execute_on_originate value could invoke the system dialplan application before answer and execute operating-system commands with the FreeSWITCH process privileges. SIP REFER is enabled by default, and the sender needs only a registered account and a call that takes the off-box transfer path, not administrative or Event Socket access. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

descriptions.description: CWE-77: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

scenarios.value: Same threat model and outcome as CVE-2026-17566, of which this is a bypass: any authenticated user with the Import/Export Data permission (granted by default) and an ordinary database role, which can set standard_conforming_strings itself, so Attack Complexity is Low. Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability are High for command execution on the pgAdmin host. Scope is Changed, as for CVE-2026-17566, because the command runs on the pgAdmin host rather than within the database server the user is connected to.

Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry and the same vector as CVE-2026-17566. AT:N because no condition outside the attacker's control is needed. VC/VI/VA:H for the pgAdmin host and SC/SI/SA:H for the systems reachable from it with its credentials.

descriptions.value:
pgAdmin 4's Import/Export Data tool wraps a user's query export in a psql \copy (...) TO command and checks that the query's parentheses are balanced so that nothing can escape the wrapper. The check rejected a backslash inside a single-quoted string, but not inside a double-quoted identifier, where it treated the next double quote as closing the identifier. psql's \copy parser applies the connection's escape character to whichever quote opened a token, so with standard_conforming_strings off a backslash-escaped double quote does not close the identifier. pgAdmin's and psql's view of the quoting then diverged, a closing parenthesis hidden from the check ended the \copy (...) wrapper, and a following TO PROGRAM clause was executed by psql on the pgAdmin host, as the operating-system account running pgAdmin, before the server rejected the statement. An ordinary database role can turn standard_conforming_strings off for itself, and the Import/Export Data permission is granted to non-administrators by default.

This is a bypass of the fix for CVE-2026-17566. The fix rejects any backslash inside a double-quoted identifier, as was already done for single-quoted strings, since its meaning depends on a server setting that cannot be known reliably when the query is validated.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

cna.title: Widget Options <= 4.2.6.1 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Code Injection via 'post_content' Parameter

affected.product: Widget Options – Advanced Conditional Visibility for Gutenberg Blocks & Classic Widgets

descriptions.value: The Widget Options – Advanced Conditional Visibility for Gutenberg Blocks & Classic Widgets plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Code Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.6.1 via the `post_content` parameter. This is due to asymmetric parsing between the save-time strip filter (`widgetopts_strip_logic_from_blocks()`) and the render-time parser (`blockopts_filter_before_display()`): embedding an inner `<!--start_widgetopts` literal inside a JSON key causes the write-side `json_decode` to see a non-`class` key and skip stripping — persisting the payload verbatim to the database — while the render-side `str_replace` reconstitutes the key to `class`, feeding the attacker-controlled `logic` value directly into `@eval`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to inject PHP expressions that execute on every front-end page view, enabling boolean-oracle exfiltration of WordPress site configuration data — including admin email address, default role, and arbitrary `get_option`, `get_user_meta`, and `get_post_meta` values — via the plugin's allowlisted-function sandbox, which escalates to unrestricted code execution if any installed plugin extends the `widgetopts_allowed_php_functions` filter. Contributors can also exploit this vulnerability when their submitted post is later published by an administrator; notably, the injected payload executes for all site visitors, including unauthenticated users, because a trust-flag mechanism introduced in version 4.2.6 causes `widgetopts_safe_eval_trusted()` to bypass its non-admin short-circuit at every legacy render callsite. Exploitation by attackers with contributor-level access and above requires that an administrator (or editor) later publishes the contributor's submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

cna.title: MISP Guard Case-Sensitive Policy Bypass Allows Unauthorized Feed Data Forwarding

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [security] match categories and required taxonomies

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [security] match categories and required taxonomies
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix makes all policy-matching comparisons case-insensitive by applying .lower() to both the input value (tag name, attribute category, sharing-group UUID) and the configured policy value (required taxonomy prefix, allowed tags, blocked categories, blocked UUIDs) before performing the comparison. This ensures that a tag such as 'TLP:AMBER' is correctly recognized as belonging to the 'tlp' taxonomy and is checked against the allowed-tags list, and that a blocked category or UUID is matched regardless of letter case.
assumptions: The MISP Guard is assumed to operate as a proxy filtering outbound MISP feed data; the attacker is assumed to have the ability to create or modify events in a MISP instance that feeds through the guard. The patch does not specify the exact deployment topology.

PR:L assumes that creating events in MISP requires at least a low-privilege authenticated account. If the guard is used in a context where events are pushed from a connected MISP instance without per-event authentication, PR could be None.
The CAPEC-10 mapping is the closest available pattern; the actual attack involves modifying structured JSON event fields rather than traditional HTTP parameters, so the mapping is approximate.
No specific affected or fixed version numbers are provided in the patch metadata; the version range is marked as unspecified.

The commit message references 'ID 004' as a prior related fix, suggesting this is a follow-up to an earlier incomplete case-sensitivity fix, but no further details about that prior fix are available in the patch.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In src/mispguard.py, four comparison sites were changed: (1) check_required_taxonomy_exists now uses tag['name'].lower().startswith(required_taxonomy.lower() + ':') instead of a case-sensitive startswith; (2) check_required_taxonomy_tags_allowed applies .lower() to both the tag name and the required taxonomy prefix in the startswith check; (3) check_blocked_attribute_categories compares attribute['category'].lower() against a lowercased list of blocked categories; (4) check_blocked_analyst_data_sharing_groups_uuids compares the UUID in lowercase against a lowercased list of blocked UUIDs. Ninety-one lines of test cases were added to src/test/test_misp_guard.py covering mixed-case TLP tags in required-taxonomy checks and mixed-case blocked attribute categories.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The MISP feed is consumed over the network (HTTP). AC:L: Exploitation requires only changing the letter case of a tag, category, or UUID string. AT:N: No log or audit tampering is needed. PR:L: The attacker needs the ability to create or modify events in a MISP instance, which typically requires a low-privilege user account or a connected instance. UI:N: No user interaction is required. VC:H: The primary impact is unauthorized disclosure of data that the operator intended to restrict (non-allowed TLP tags, blocked categories, blocked sharing groups are forwarded to feed consumers). VI:N: The data content is not modified, only improperly shared. VA:N: No availability impact. SC/SI/SA:N: No secondary system impact is evidenced.

capecRationale.rationale: The attacker tampers with the letter case of tag names, attribute categories, or sharing-group UUIDs in MISP events to bypass the guard's policy checks. This is a form of parameter tampering where the input is modified in a way that the validation logic does not anticipate. CAPEC-10 is the closest available pattern; the uncertainty is that the tampering occurs in structured event data rather than in a traditional request parameter, but the underlying technique (modifying input to evade validation) aligns with this pattern.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The root cause is that string comparisons used to enforce security policies (taxonomy prefix matching, category blocking, UUID blocking) were case-sensitive, allowing an attacker to bypass the checks by altering letter case. CWE-178 is the most specific and accurate mapping.
More broadly, the guard failed to validate input against the policy in a canonical form, which is a form of improper input validation. CWE-20 is included as a secondary, broader mapping.

events.description: Corrective change authored (9868b1d93fc9cc40cc7c69ca11c86afd825bbc1c): fix: [security] match categories and required taxonomies

descriptions.value: CAPEC-10 Parameter Tampering

solutions.value: The fix makes all policy-matching comparisons case-insensitive by applying .lower() to both the input value (tag name, attribute category, sharing-group UUID) and the configured policy value (required taxonomy prefix, allowed tags, blocked categories, blocked UUIDs) before performing the comparison. This ensures that a tag such as 'TLP:AMBER' is correctly recognized as belonging to the 'tlp' taxonomy and is checked against the allowed-tags list, and that a blocked category or UUID is matched regardless of letter case.

supportingMedia.value: The fix makes all policy-matching comparisons case-insensitive by applying .lower() to both the input value (tag name, attribute category, sharing-group UUID) and the configured policy value (required taxonomy prefix, allowed tags, blocked categories, blocked UUIDs) before performing the comparison. This ensures that a tag such as 'TLP:AMBER' is correctly recognized as belonging to the 'tlp' taxonomy and is checked against the allowed-tags list, and that a blocked category or UUID is matched regardless of letter case.

descriptions.value:
MISP Guard, a proxy-based security filter for MISP feed distribution, contains a case-sensitivity flaw in multiple policy enforcement checks. The functions check_required_taxonomy_exists, check_required_taxonomy_tags_allowed, check_blocked_attribute_categories, and check_blocked_analyst_data_sharing_groups_uuids performed case-sensitive string comparisons when matching event tags, attribute categories, and sharing-group UUIDs against configured allow/block lists.

An attacker with the ability to create or modify events in a MISP instance (or a connected instance that pushes events through the guard) could craft events using different letter case in taxonomy tag names, attribute categories, or sharing-group UUIDs to bypass the configured security policies. For example, if the policy requires the 'tlp' taxonomy with only 'tlp:clear' allowed, an event tagged 'TLP:AMBER' would not be recognized as belonging to the 'tlp' taxonomy and would therefore not be checked against the allowed-tags list, resulting in the event being forwarded to feed consumers. Similarly, a blocked attribute category such as 'Person' would not match a configured block entry of 'person', allowing the attribute to pass through the filter.

The security impact is unauthorized disclosure of threat-intelligence data that the operator intended to restrict. Events carrying non-allowed TLP (Traffic Light Protocol) markings, blocked attribute categories, or blocked sharing-group associations are forwarded to downstream feed consumers in violation of the configured distribution policy. This undermines the confidentiality controls that MISP Guard is designed to enforce.

The vulnerability is trivially exploitable: the attacker only needs to alter the letter case of a tag, category, or UUID string. No authentication beyond normal MISP event-creation privileges is required, and no user interaction is needed.

cna.title: pgAdmin 4: File Manager and storage-path tools act on a different path from the one checked

scenarios.value: Scored for the worst variant, which needs only an authenticated user in server mode: reading any file the pgAdmin account can read through the Query Tool's file open, and listing any directory. Attack Complexity is Low. Confidentiality is High because that includes pgAdmin's own configuration and database. Integrity is None for this variant; the read, delete and rename of another user's files need a deployment where one user's storage directory name is a prefix of another's, and the write outside storage is limited to Windows server mode. Scope is Unchanged: the access is with the authority of the pgAdmin account.
Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry. AT:N for the any-file read, which needs no deployment condition. VC:H; no subsequent-system impact is claimed.

descriptions.value:
In server mode pgAdmin 4 validates a path into the user's storage directory with check_access_permission(), which builds the absolute path with get_abs_path(). Several callers then acted on a path they built differently, so the path checked and the path used could name different files:

- Opening a file in the Query Tool, the Google client secret and, on Windows, Import/Export Data, Backup, Restore and saving a file joined the path to the storage directory after stripping leading slashes and backslashes. On POSIX a path checked as a name inside storage could become an absolute path once stripped, so any file the pgAdmin account can read could be opened; on Windows a path naming a drive discarded the storage directory, so these could read, or write, outside it.
- Listing a folder decoded the path a second time after the check, so a folder named like an encoded "..", which a user can create, listed any directory on the host.
- Download, delete, rename and the file-exists check appended the path to the storage directory without a separator, so in a deployment where one user's storage directory name is a prefix of another's, another user's files could be read, deleted or moved; download also checked the path appended to itself.
- Creating a folder could create one in another user's directory.

The fix makes check_access_permission() return the path it checked and every caller act on that path, decodes folder paths once, and opens, deletes and renames files relative to directories opened from the storage directory without following symbolic links. Desktop mode is not affected.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

cna.title: FileBrowser Quantum: Symlink following escapes user scope allowing arbitrary file read outside the served directory

descriptions.value: FileBrowser Quantum is a free, self-hosted, web-based file manager. Prior to 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta, file read handling in backend/pkg/indexing/indexingFiles.go resolves symbolic links through GetRealPath without confirming that the resolved target remains inside the source root and the user's authorized scope. Download, preview, media, OnlyOffice, and public-share read flows that enable FollowSymlinks can therefore serve an out-of-scope target through a reachable in-scope symlink. An authenticated user with download access can read server-accessible files outside the assigned scope, and a holder of a public share link can do the same without an account when the shared directory exposes such a symlink. This issue is fixed in 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta.

From 2.19.0 until 3.17.0, mlflow.crewai.autolog() records CrewAI Agent objects without consistently sanitizing nested credential-bearing values. mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_get_agent_attributes() converts the Agent llm field to a string that includes the provider API key, while mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_construct_full_inputs() expands the Agent object into mlflow.spanInputs. Applications can therefore send plaintext provider credentials to the MLflow trace backend or a configured OTLP destination, where trace readers can obtain them. This issue is fixed in version 3.17.0.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication heap out-of-bounds write in mod_xml_rpc WebSocket frame length handling

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, ws_read_frame() decoded a WebSocket frame's 64-bit extended payload length with a 32-bit byte swap and narrowed the result into a signed length. A value whose surviving low word became negative bypassed the signed size check and was reinterpreted as an enormous unsigned count, causing client bytes to overwrite memory beyond the 64 KiB receive buffer. Any client completing a /socket WebSocket upgrade on an enabled mod_xml_rpc endpoint reached the parser before HTTP authentication; both the module and WebSocket endpoint are disabled by default. The heap overwrite can corrupt connection pointers and crash FreeSWITCH, ending every concurrent session, although remote code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

cna.title: HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl lose track of chunk boundaries in chunked request bodies when a read ends inside a chunk

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Body 1.23_01 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.23_01 for Perl lose track of chunk boundaries in chunked request bodies when a read ends inside a chunk.

In chunked mode, used when no content length is given, add() treats a chunk as complete once the buffer is as long as the chunk's declared size, but the buffer still holds the chunk-size line. When a read ends in the last bytes of a chunk, add() takes the chunk short and parses the leftover data as the next chunk-size line.

A remote attacker can make a chunked body never complete, hanging a server that reads until the body is done, and may make it complete early, leaving the remaining bytes to be read as the next request.

cna.title: HTTP::Parser::XS versions before 0.18 for Perl truncate PATH_INFO at an encoded NUL byte in parse_http_request

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Parser-XS 0.18 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Parser::XS versions before 0.18 for Perl truncate PATH_INFO at an encoded NUL byte in parse_http_request.

The XS parser URL-decodes the request path and measures the result with strlen(), so PATH_INFO ends at the first byte decoded from %00. The pure-Perl backend is not affected.

A remote attacker can send a path that a proxy or filter checks in full while the application routes on a shorter one.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH mod_sofia: stack buffer overflow from an over-long SIP Contact display-name

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is an open-source software telecommunications platform. From 1.10.0 to 1.11.1, there is a stack-based buffer overflow in  mod_sofia  when processing SIP Contact display names for dialog-event notifications. A peer can establish a dialog containing an excessively long display name and subsequently subscribe to that entity’s dialog events, causing the stored value to overflow a fixed 512-byte stack buffer. Exploitation requires presence management to be enabled, directly or through shared appearance, and normally requires valid profile credentials unless subscription authentication is disabled. The overflow can terminate the FreeSWITCH process and all active calls. This vulnerability is fixed in version 1.11.2.

cna.title: russh's SSH agent server is susceptible to unbound allocations via repeated SSH_AGENT_CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM messages

descriptions.value: russh is a Rust SSH client and server library that includes an SSH agent protocol implementation. Prior to 0.65.0, russh::keys::agent::server::serve in russh/src/keys/agent/server.rs accepts repeated SSH_AGENT_CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM records while adding a key and appends every Constraint::Confirm record to the key's retained constraint vector without a count or memory limit. A process that can connect to the agent socket, including the remote side of a forwarded agent session, can repeatedly add constrained keys and cause renewable memory growth that persists for the process lifetime because keys without a lifetime constraint do not expire. This issue is fixed in version 0.65.0.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Inbound SIP MESSAGE can select the api chat proto and run FreeSWITCH API commands

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.3, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() split the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on a plus sign and treated the left side as a chat protocol selector. Selecting the api chat proto reached switch_api_execute(), allowing a peer whose MESSAGE was accepted to run FreeSWITCH API commands, including operating-system command sinks, with the daemon's privileges. Inbound chat is enabled on the stock internal and external profiles, and any authenticated profile account is sufficient; stock directory users without password material can also remove that barrier in affected configurations. The flaw permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution, and exploitation has been observed in the wild. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.3.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication invalid pointer dereference in mod_rtmp connect command handling

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, rtmp_i_connect() passed the first RTMP connect argument to amf0_object_get() without checking whether the AMF value was an object. A string or number in place of an AMF object caused union bytes from the message to be interpreted as node pointers and dereferenced. Any client with network access to an enabled mod_rtmp listener could send the malformed connect command before login; the module is disabled in the stock build and configuration. The invalid read reliably crashes FreeSWITCH and ends every active call, while no write, memory disclosure, or code execution has been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

cna.title: WP Visitor Statistics (Real Time Traffic) <= 8.8 - Authenticated (Contributor+) SQL Injection via 'from' Shortcode Attribute

descriptions.value: The WP Visitor Statistics (Real Time Traffic) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'from' (and sibling 'to'/'first'/'second') shortcode attribute of the [wsm_showTrafficStatsList] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 8.8 This is due to insufficient escaping on the user-supplied attribute and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query: `shortcode_atts()` returns attacker-supplied shortcode attributes verbatim (WP core performs no sanitization), only `$atts['id']` is re-sanitized afterward, and the raw value is then concatenated into a double-quoted SQL string literal inside `fnGetHourlyReportByDateNameTimeZone()` (`includes/wsm_db.php:1449`) and executed via `$wpdb->get_results()`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

cna.title: systeminformation: Windows command injection in services() through Unicode quotation marks

descriptions.value: systeminformation is a System and OS information library for node.js. Prior to 5.33.16, services() in lib/processes.js inserts a caller-supplied service name into a PowerShell Get-CimInstance filter after processing it with sanitizeShellString() in lib/util.js. On Windows, the sanitizer removes ASCII quotes but permits Unicode quotation marks that PowerShell accepts as string delimiters, allowing crafted input to terminate the filter and place a PowerShell expression in the command executed by util.powerShell(). The expression runs with the Node.js process account's permissions and may read or change accessible files, alter application data, or disrupt the service. The package does not expose a network service itself, so remote reachability depends on a consuming application forwarding attacker-controlled input to services() or getDynamicData(). This issue is fixed in version 5.33.16.
