cna.title: pgAdmin 4: Materialized view refresh redirects its connection through a crafted database name

scenarios.value: Same threat model and vector as CVE-2026-86862, of which this is the remaining caller. The attacker needs a database role with CREATEDB on a server another pgAdmin user connects to, and that user must refresh a materialized view in that database; no other precondition applies, so Attack Complexity is Low. Confidentiality is High because the victim's saved server password is sent to the attacker's endpoint. Integrity and Availability are None. Scope is Unchanged, as for CVE-2026-86862: the credential is captured from the user's own connection rather than a different authority being exercised.

Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry. AT:N because no condition outside the attacker's control is needed beyond the victim using the feature. VC:H for the captured password; no subsequent-system impact is claimed from the flaw itself.

descriptions.value:
pgAdmin 4's materialized view refresh passed the target database's name to psql's --dbname argument unchanged. libpq treats a --dbname value containing "=" (or a postgresql:// URI) as a full connection string, whose keywords override the host, port and other settings pgAdmin had supplied. A database whose name is such a string, which any role with CREATEDB can create, therefore redirected the psql process pgAdmin starts for the refresh to a host and port of the creator's choosing, and the connecting user's saved server password was presented to that endpoint. It also let the pgAdmin host be made to open connections to arbitrary addresses.

The same weakness was fixed for Backup, Restore, Maintenance and Import/Export Data in earlier releases (CVE-2026-86862); the materialized view refresh was the remaining caller. The fix routes the name through the same database_conninfo() helper, so libpq treats it strictly as a database name.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

cna.title: russh: peer-declared zero maximum packet size permanently stalls channel writes (silent AsyncWrite hang)

descriptions.value: russh is a Rust SSH client and server library that includes an SSH agent protocol implementation. From 0.60.0 until 0.65.0, channel-open parsing accepts a peer-declared maximum_packet_size of zero and passes it into ChannelTx::poll_writable in russh/src/channels/io/tx.rs. The Channel::data, Channel::make_writer, and Channel::into_stream asynchronous write paths then calculate a writable size of zero and remain pending forever because window adjustments cannot satisfy a static zero packet maximum. An authenticated client can strand server writes, and a malicious server can strand client writes, allowing affected tasks, channels, and connections to accumulate without surfacing an error. cna.title: undici vulnerable to cross-user information disclosure via cross-origin redirect revalidation

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, when an Agent composes the redirect and shared cache interceptors, a cached response that is revalidated with a conditional request can be validated by a 304 Not Modified from a different origin. When the origin that stored the response redirects the conditional revalidation request to another origin, the redirect handler strips origin-bound credential headers but not the cache-generated If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since validators, so the redirect destination receives the original origin's validator and undici treats its 304 as successful revalidation of the stored representation. As a result, a shared cache can serve the original origin's stored authenticated response, including one gated by Authorization, to a later unauthenticated caller. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, compose the interceptors as cache then redirect, use per-origin dispatchers and cache stores, or disable shared caching on redirect-capable requests.

Attackers can use the public anonymous CSRF token to read internal store statistics, enqueue jobs like smw.entityIdDisposer, and execute queued jobs, degrading performance and altering semantic data.

cna.title: USB Test: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in getSectorSize via untrusted DISK_GEOMETRY.BytesPerSector leads to RCE/DoS

descriptions.value: USB Test is a lightweight Windows CLI utility for verifying sector integrity and detecting overreported capacity on USB flash drives. Prior to version 1.1.5, getSectorSize() in USB Test/src/driveinfo.cpp trusts DISK_GEOMETRY.BytesPerSector returned by IOCTL_DISK_GET_DRIVE_GEOMETRY without checking whether the call succeeded or enforcing size bounds. USB Test/src/drivetest.cpp uses the value for division and to size a heap buffer before memcpy(buffer.data(), &sector, 8), so a physically connected malicious USB storage device can report a value below eight bytes and cause repeated out-of-bounds writes, or report zero and cause a divide-by-zero denial of service when a user starts a drive test. The heap corruption can crash the elevated application and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.5.

cna.title: SEOPress <= 10.3 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'display_name' Profile Field via %%archive_title%% Template Tag

affected.product: SEOPress – AI SEO Plugin & On-site SEO

descriptions.value: The SEOPress – AI SEO Plugin & On-site SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'display_name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 10.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by any Subscriber who sets their display_name to a string containing the literal %%archive_title%% token alongside HTML event-handler payloads, as WordPress stores display names without HTML filtering and the plugin substitutes the token after escaping has already occurred.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

cna.title: Atlantis: OS command injection through PR-controlled Terraform workspace enables RCE during plan

descriptions.value: Atlantis is a self-hosted golang application that listens for Terraform pull request events via webhooks. From version 0.4.0 until 0.47.1, Atlantis passes the pull-request-controlled workspace value from atlantis.yaml into Terraform command arguments that are joined with strings.Join(args, " ") and executed through sh -c. An authenticated contributor whose pull request is eligible for an Atlantis plan can include shell metacharacters in the workspace name, causing arbitrary commands to execute as the Atlantis service account without custom workflows, apply permission, or a malicious Terraform provider. External contributors can reach the flaw through fork pull requests only when --allow-fork-prs is enabled, while eligible same-repository branches do not require that option. The commands inherit the Atlantis process environment and can access cloud-provider, Terraform, and version-control credentials as well as files, state, and network resources available to the service. This issue is fixed in version 0.47.1.

descriptions.description: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

cna.title: pgAdmin 4: Server passwords are left in pgAdmin's process environment

scenarios.value: Requires the PSQL tool to be enabled (ENABLE_PSQL) and another user to have used it (User Interaction Required), and the attacker's connection or utility to follow in the same pgAdmin process (Attack Complexity High). The gain is real only for users without the PSQL tool permission: a user who has it already holds a shell as the pgAdmin account. Scope is Changed because the password belongs to another user; Confidentiality is High for it. Integrity is Low, reflecting that the attacker's use of the other user's database identity is constrained by these conditions; Availability is None.

Same reasoning as the CVSS 3.1 entry. AT:P for the timing and configuration conditions, UI:P because the victim only has to use the PSQL tool. VC:H for the leaked password; SC:H/SI:L for the database server it opens.

descriptions.value:
To pass a server's password to psql and to the utilities pgAdmin 4 runs as background processes, the server manager wrote it into pgAdmin's own process environment: as PGPASSWORD for the PSQL tool, and under a per-process variable for a utility. Nothing removed it afterwards. pgAdmin's environment is shared by every user's requests and copied into every process it starts, so in server mode another user's later PSQL session or utility inherited the password, and libpq used PGPASSWORD for any connection made without a password of its own, letting one user connect with another user's saved password.

The fix puts the password only into the environment built for the process that needs it and starts psql with a copy of pgAdmin's environment instead of the environment itself.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

descriptions.value: SGLang through 0.5.23, fixed in commit 7b5fb39, contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the POST /load_lora_adapter_from_tensors HTTP endpoint, which lacks the @auth_level(AuthLevel.ADMIN_OPTIONAL) decorator applied to its sibling admin endpoints, allowing unauthenticated network-reachable attackers to invoke it without an API key. cna.title: Permission bypass through editing scheduled exports

descriptions.value:
When changing the settings of a scheduled export, no permission checks are done to see whether the user making the change has access to the exporter after the change. This way, an attacker with access to change organizer settings and e.g. access to all orders could change the export to refer to gift cards instead, even if they do not have access to gift cards.




The fix for this is technically a breaking API change, since changing the export type of existing scheduled exports is no longer allowed, but we don't expect this to affect any typical API usage.

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [website] authorize external tool management
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: A before_request authorization handler is added to the external_tools blueprint that checks whether the admin user is active (ADMIN_PASSWORD configured) and whether the current user is authenticated before any management endpoint executes. When both conditions indicate an unauthenticated request to a protected endpoint, the handler redirects to the login page (for the add endpoint) or returns a 403 Permission Denied response (for delete, status, and configuration endpoints). This enforces the same optional-admin policy already applied to module configuration, while preserving the existing open-management behavior when no admin password is configured.
assumptions: The CAPEC mapping to CAPEC-1 (Software Feature Discovery) is the closest available pattern; no CAPEC specifically models exploitation of a missing authorization check on a discovered endpoint. The mapping is uncertain but is the best fit given the attack sequence of discovering and then invoking unauthenticated management endpoints.

CVSS SI:H assumes that external tools in MISP feed into a broader data ingestion pipeline whose integrity is affected by unauthorized modification of tool configurations. If external tools are isolated to a single instance with no downstream consumers, SI could be reduced.
The vulnerability is conditional on ADMIN_PASSWORD being configured. Installations without ADMIN_PASSWORD intentionally allow open management access by design and are not considered vulnerable.
No specific version boundaries are identified in the patch; the affected version range is unspecified.
The patch references issue #816 in the MISP/misp-modules repository, but no additional context about the issue tracker entry is available to confirm reporter or finder credits.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: The patch adds a before_request decorator on external_tools_blueprint in website/app/external_tools/external_tools.py that imports current_user from flask_login and admin_user_active from app.utils. The handler checks if the request endpoint is one of the four management endpoints (add_external_tool, delete_tool, change_status, change_config) and if the admin user is active but the current user is not authenticated, it either redirects to the login page or returns a 403 JSON response. The patch also adds a new test file website/tests/external_tools_checks.py with regression tests verifying that anonymous mutations are denied even with valid CSRF tokens, that authorization precedes JSON validation, that authenticated admins can perform all operations, and that the open-management policy is preserved when no admin password is set. The README is updated to document the new authorization requirement.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The vulnerability is exploitable over the network via HTTP requests to the website. AC:L: No special conditions are required; standard HTTP POST/GET requests to known endpoints suffice. AT:N: No attack target manipulation is needed. PR:N: No privileges are required; the attack works as an anonymous user. UI:N: No user interaction is required. VC:L: Tool configurations including API keys and URLs are accessible/modifiable by the attacker. VI:H: The attacker can add, delete, and modify external tools, fully compromising the integrity of the tool management function. VA:L: Deleting or disabling tools reduces availability of data ingestion. SC:N: No secondary system confidentiality impact identified. SI:H: External tools feed into the broader MISP data pipeline; modifying them can corrupt or redirect data ingestion for the entire MISP instance. SA:N: No secondary availability impact beyond the direct effect.

capecRationale.rationale: The closest available CAPEC pattern is Software Feature Discovery, as the attacker must identify the external tools management endpoints (e.g., /add_external_tool, /external_tools/<id>/delete_tool, /external_tools/change_status, /external_tools/change_config) and then issue unauthenticated requests to them. The vulnerability is exploited by discovering that these management functions are accessible without the authorization that the application's own documentation and parallel module-configuration endpoints imply. No CAPEC specifically models 'missing authorization on a discovered endpoint,' so CAPEC-1 is the best available match for the discovery-and-exploitation sequence.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The external tools management endpoints (add, delete, change_status, change_config) lacked an authorization check that would verify the requester is an authenticated administrator when the admin-login policy is active. The authentication mechanism (flask_login, ADMIN_PASSWORD) existed in the application but was not applied to these specific endpoints, allowing anonymous users to perform privileged management operations.

descriptions.value: The MISP Modules website component exposes external tool management endpoints (add, delete, change status, and change configuration) that did not enforce the optional administrator authentication policy. When ADMIN_PASSWORD was configured in the application environment, the module configuration endpoints correctly required an authenticated administrator session, but the external tools management handlers processed requests from anonymous users without any authorization check. This inconsistency allowed bypass of the intended access control for the external tools management functionality. The vulnerability is conditional on ADMIN_PASSWORD being set; installations without an admin password intentionally permit open management access by design. The affected component is the external_tools Flask blueprint within the MISP Modules website application.

cna.title: MCUboot image hash span is not bounded against the slot, allowing a read past the flash area during image validation

descriptions.value:
bootutil_img_hash() computes the image digest over ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size + ih_protect_tlv_size bytes, all three taken from the candidate image's header, and reads that span out of the slot without checking that it fits in the flash area. The three sizes are also summed without an overflow check. Nothing earlier on the validation path bounds the whole span either: bootutil_img_validate() compares the image size against bootutil_max_image_size() only after the hash has been computed.

The callers bound part of the span, or none of it:

On the swap and overwrite upgrade path, boot_validate_slot() first runs the image header check (boot_is_header_valid(), later boot_check_header_valid()). Before MCUboot 2.2.0 that check covered only ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size, so for every image the protected-TLV area (ih_protect_tlv_size, a uint16_t, up to 65535 bytes) was hashed without being bounded. From 2.2.0 the check includes ih_protect_tlv_size, except for a compressed image in the secondary slot when MCUBOOT_DECOMPRESS_IMAGES (CONFIG_BOOT_DECOMPRESSION) is enabled, which leaves the same gap of up to 64 KB.
Zephyr's single-slot and firmware loaders (boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, boot/zephyr/firmware_loader.c) read the header with boot_image_load_header(), which bounds ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size against the flash area. Before MCUboot 2.4.0 that bound did not include ih_protect_tlv_size, which leaves the same gap of up to 64 KB. From 2.4.0 these loaders bound the whole span.
The serial recovery image-list and image-state handlers (bs_list() and bs_set() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c) call bootutil_img_validate() with no header check at all, so on those paths ih_img_size is unbounded as well.

The image is hashed before its signature is checked, so anyone who can place an image in a slot (an OTA or SMP update delivered through the application, or serial recovery) reaches this read before authentication.

Whether a malformed header produces an actual read beyond the area depends on the flash backend:

Backends whose flash_area_read() bounds-checks the request (Zephyr, Espressif, NuttX, Mbed) return an error once the chunked read crosses the end of the area. Validation fails and the image is rejected, with no over-read.
With MCUBOOT_HASH_STORAGE_DIRECTLY (Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_IMG_HASH_DIRECTLY_ON_STORAGE, available from 2.2.0, not enabled by default) the span is hashed through a single direct pointer into memory-mapped flash, with no bounds check.
The Cypress PSoC6 port's flash_area_read() (boot/cypress/cy_flash_pal/cy_flash_map.c, from 1.6.0) does not bound the read: its assert()s compare against the area's absolute offset rather than its size, and it copies with memcpy().

The bytes read past the area feed only the digest, which is compared internally and never returned, so nothing is disclosed. The realistic effect is a read fault during image validation: up to 64 KB past the slot on the upgrade path and, before 2.4.0, on the Zephyr loaders, and potentially much further on the serial recovery handlers, which skip the header check. Where validation is repeated at every boot (a pending upgrade, or, before 2.4.0, the single-slot loader checking its image), the fault can recur on each reset and keep the device from booting.

The fix makes bootutil_img_hash() add the three sizes with boot_u32_safe_add() and reject an image whose span, including the sector offset used in swap-using-offset mode, does not fit in the flash area, before any of it is hashed. Because the bound is applied where the bytes are read, it covers every caller.

cna.title: Circumvention of offline barcode revocation check in pretixSCAN

descriptions.value:
pretix provides a mechanism where ticket QR codes are cryptographically signed and can be verified by our pretixSCAN apps in offline mode without any database of valid tickets. pretixSCAN checks the signature to verify that the ticket was issued by the correct pretix event and compares the QR code against a list of revoked QR codes. A QR code becomes revoked when the order is canceled, or the ticket is changed in a way that a new QR code needs to be generated.




However, the parsing of the QR code in all of our pretixSCAN apps contained a faulty computation, rendering the check for the correct length of the contents faulty. This way, an attacker is able to craft multiple QR codes for the same ticket which have the same content, but look different and therefore do not match against the revocation list. This does not allow to fabricate entirely new tickets, but it does allow to enter the event with e.g. a canceled ticket. This attack requires pretixSCAN to be scanning in offline mode and the "pretix signature scheme 1" to be used for the event's QR codes.




If the attack is executed, the ticket unfortunately shows as valid (green) on the scanner but as invalid (red) on the server since the server later cannot match it to a ticket. We scanned the entire database of scans on pretix Hosted and could not find any traces of this being exploited in the past.

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Jiawei Guo for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Build execution environments only from trusted collection sources. Review the contents of requirements.txt files from untrusted or third-party collections before running ansible-builder build or introspect.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in ansible-builder. The regular expression used to strip comments from a collection's requirements.txt during introspection is susceptible to super-quadratic backtracking. A requirements file containing a line with a long run of internal whitespace and no comment character causes the comment-stripping routine to consume CPU time proportional to the square of the line length. An attacker who can get a victim to build an execution environment that includes an attacker-supplied collection can cause the ansible-builder build or introspect process to hang, resulting in a denial of service. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.

content.description: GnuTLS severity rating: Low. Exploitation requires an allocation failure to happen at a specific call during name constraints reinitialization.

exploits.value: Exploitation has only been observed under precise allocation failure injection.

solutions.value: Backport upstream commit "x509: make name constraints deinitialization idempotent", or update to GnuTLS 3.8.14.

descriptions.value: A double free in the X.509 name constraints enforcement of GnuTLS 3.8.13 on all platforms allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a certificate chain containing a NameConstraints extension processed while the application is under memory pressure. When an already populated name constraints object is reinitialized, previously freed list pointers are not cleared, so a memory allocation failure precisely at reinitialization leaves a dangling pointer that is freed again during a later cleanup.

cna.title: TLV iterator does not bound each entry against the declared TLV area in MCUboot bootutil

descriptions.value:
The MCUboot TLV iterator bootutil_tlv_iter_next() in boot/bootutil/src/tlv.c walks image trailer TLVs with a single loop guard (it->tlv_off < it->tlv_end) and advances by sizeof(struct image_tlv) + tlv.it_len using the attacker-controlled it_len field, without validating that the entry's header or payload stays within it->tlv_end. As a result the 4-byte header read can extend up to 3 bytes past the declared TLV area, and the returned (off, len) can describe a payload that runs past it.

The path is pre-authentication: TLVs are parsed during bootutil_img_validate() before the signature is verified, and a crafted image can be presented through DFU / serial-recovery / OTA. However the impact is contained by surrounding guards: bootutil_img_validate() first rejects a TLV area larger than bootutil_max_image_size(), the default LOAD_IMAGE_DATA sink is flash_area_read() which bounds-checks against the flash partition and fails an out-of-partition read, and every payload consumer (EXPECTED_HASH_TLV, EXPECTED_KEY_TLV, EXPECTED_SIG_TLV, IMAGE_TLV_SEC_CNT) clamps len against a fixed buffer before copying.

The residual effect in a default flash build is therefore an out-of-region read confined to the attacker's own slot partition whose result is never observable, yielding at worst a clean validation failure rather than memory corruption or information disclosure. A genuine (though still bounded) out-of-bounds read remains under the non-default MCUBOOT_RAM_LOAD configuration, where LOAD_IMAGE_DATA is an unchecked memcpy. The fix is to validate each entry's header and payload against it->tlv_end inside the iterator.

cna.title: MISP Modules Website Exposes External Tool API Keys in /external_tools/list Response

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [website] keep external tool API keys out of responses

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [website] keep external tool API keys out of responses
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix removes the api_key field from the ExternalTools.to_json() serializer so that /external_tools/list no longer returns credentials. The edit form is changed to a write-only pattern: the API key input starts empty, a blank or missing value on save retains the previously stored key, and a non-empty value replaces it. After a successful save the client clears the key field and does not propagate the credential into the in-memory tool list. Input validation is tightened to reject non-string or over-length key values. Server-side tool submissions continue to use the stored key from the database.
assumptions: The /external_tools/list endpoint is accessible without authentication based on regression tests that verify the response for both authenticated and unauthenticated clients; however, the README notes that management operations require ADMIN_PASSWORD, so the list endpoint's access control may vary by deployment configuration.
CVSS SC:H assumes the exposed API keys grant meaningful access to external services; the actual scope of access depends on the specific external tools configured and is not specified in the patch.
No specific product version or release boundary is identified in the patch; the affected version range is therefore marked as unspecified.

CAPEC-126 is the closest available pattern but is not a perfect match; the vulnerability is more precisely an API response information disclosure than a session hijacking. No CAPEC pattern specifically covers 'sensitive credential in API JSON response' without a session framing.
The commit references issue #816 but no reporter or finder is named in the patch metadata or commit message.

The 60-character maximum length validation for API keys is a new constraint introduced by the patch; it is unclear whether keys longer than 60 characters were previously valid, which could affect deployments with longer keys.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: models.py: removed the api_key entry from ExternalTools.to_json(). external_tools.py (change_config endpoint): replaced the nested if-chain that required tool_api_key to be present and non-empty with a flat validation loop for tool_id/tool_name/tool_url, added a type-and-length check (string, max 60 chars) for tool_api_key when present, and made the field optional (write-only semantics). external_tools_core.py (change_config_core): changed tool.api_key assignment to be conditional on a truthy request_json.get('tool_api_key'). external_tools_index.html: initialized the form key field to empty string instead of tool.api_key, added placeholder and helper text, fixed a bug where the error-clearing selector referenced the wrong field, moved browser-state updates to after a successful HTTP response (res.ok check), and cleared the key input after save. README.md: documented the write-only key behavior. Tests: added browser-level (Playwright) and unit-level regression tests verifying the list endpoint omits api_key,空
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: the /external_tools/list endpoint is reachable over the network via HTTP. AC:L: exploitation requires only a single GET request with no special conditions. AT:N: no attack prerequisites such as race conditions or specific timing. PR:N: regression tests confirm the endpoint returns 200 and previously included api_key for both authenticated and unauthenticated clients, indicating no privilege is required. UI:N: no victim interaction is needed; the attacker simply reads the response. VC:H: the exposed data is API keys (credentials) for external services, representing high confidentiality loss. VI:N and VA:N: no integrity or availability impact on the MISP Modules website. SC:H: the stolen API keys can be used to authenticate to external analysis/enrichment services, representing high confidentiality impact on a subsequent component. SI:N and SA:N: no integrity or availability impact on subsequent components is indicated.

capecRationale.rationale: The closest available CAPEC pattern. The attack involves an attacker obtaining credential material (API keys) from a web application response and using it to authenticate to a subsequent service. CAPEC-126 covers the theft of session/credential tokens from a web application. The mapping is imperfect because the keys are long-lived API credentials rather than short-lived session tokens, and the attack does not involve a session per se, but the underlying mechanism (reading a credential from an HTTP response and replaying it) is the same class of attack. No CAPEC pattern specifically covers 'sensitive data in API response' without a session-hijacking framing, so this is the best available match.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The /external_tools/list endpoint returned stored API keys in its JSON response to any client (authenticated or not), exposing credentials to unauthorized parties. The browser form also pre-populated the key in the DOM.

API keys used to authenticate to external services were stored and transmitted without adequate protection: they appeared in API responses and in client-side form state, violating the principle that credentials should be write-only from the client perspective.

descriptions.value:
The MISP Modules website component contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the external tools management interface. The /external_tools/list endpoint returned stored API keys (the api_key field) in its JSON response via the ExternalTools model serializer. Additionally, the browser-based edit form pre-populated the API key input field with the stored credential value, exposing it in the DOM.

The /external_tools/list endpoint is accessible without authentication (the regression tests verify the response for both authenticated and unauthenticated clients), meaning any network-reachable client could retrieve the API keys for all configured external tools. These keys are used by the server to authenticate submissions to external analysis or enrichment services, so their disclosure allows an attacker to impersonate the MISP instance or directly access those external services.

The vulnerability also affected the edit workflow: the change_config endpoint previously required the API key to be present and non-empty on every save, forcing the key to round-trip through the client. The browser JavaScript stored the key in a reactive state object and updated the in-memory tool list with the credential value, further increasing the window of exposure in client-side memory and network traffic.

Affected component: the website sub-application of MISP Modules, specifically the external_tools module (serializer in models.py, list endpoint, and the external_tools_index.html template). The impact is limited to confidentiality of the stored API keys; no integrity or availability impact on the MISP Modules website itself is indicated by the patch.

cna.title: NULL pointer dereference when a response fragment is not acknowledged

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 aborts the Application Relationship of an RPC session when a fragment of a response has been resent without being acknowledged, without checking that the session has an Application Relationship. A request for an existing Application Relationship that is sent on another activity than its Connect, and gets a fragmented response, is handled on a session without one. If the response is not acknowledged, a NULL pointer is dereferenced and the device crashes. A conformant IO-controller does not send such requests. The attacker must have observed the AR UUID of an established Application Relationship and requires ADJACENT network access.

cna.title: Out-of-bounds write with too many MCR blocks in a Connect request

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

workarounds.value: Build P-Net with PNET_OPTION_MC_CR disabled. Multicast communication relations are not supported by P-Net, and a Connect request with MCR blocks is then rejected.

supportingMedia.value: Build P-Net with PNET_OPTION_MC_CR disabled. Multicast communication relations are not supported by P-Net, and a Connect request with MCR blocks is then rejected.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the number of MCR request blocks in a Connect request against the number of multicast communication relations that an Application Relationship has room for (PNET_MAX_MC_CR, 1 by default). Each further block is written past the end of the array, into the rest of the Application Relationship and, with more blocks, into the following one. The written data comes from the request. No established Application Relationship is needed, and the attacker requires ADJACENT network access. Builds with PNET_OPTION_MC_CR disabled are not affected.

cna.title: AES image key left on the stack after serial-recovery encrypted-image handling in MCUboot

descriptions.value:
In MCUboot's serial-recovery encrypted-image support (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c), decrypt_image_inplace() and boot_image_validate_encrypted() each keep a stack-local struct boot_status. boot_enc_load() writes the plaintext per-image AES key into its enckey[] field. Neither function cleared this structure before returning. In addition, a decrypt failure inside the per-sector loop of decrypt_image_inplace() returned early and skipped the total_out: cleanup, which left the expanded AES key context (enc_data) on the stack as well. The error paths of boot_image_validate_encrypted() similarly skipped boot_enc_zeroize().

The affected code is built when encrypted images (MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES, Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_ENCRYPT_IMAGE) are combined with serial recovery. It runs when an encrypted image is uploaded to the primary slot over the recovery protocol, and when the image list or state is queried while an encrypted image is in the secondary slot. After these functions return, the image's AES content key remains in dead stack memory. An attacker who can later read device RAM, for example through a debug port or retained RAM, can recover it.

This weakens the confidentiality of image-encryption keys within the bootloader trust boundary. A recovered key exposes the plaintext of the encrypted firmware image it protects. The device's long-term private decryption key is not exposed. No remote or recovery-protocol channel that returns this memory is known, so exploitation requires a separate memory-read capability.

cna.title: Remote Code Execution in LMS

descriptions.value: CAPEC-242 Code Injection

LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via unrestricted upload of dangerous file types in the service ticket feature of the client panel. The application does not verify the type or name of files attached to service tickets. An authenticated attacker can upload an .htaccess file to bypass the access restrictions on the storage directory, together with a PHP script. Visiting the uploaded PHP file's URL leads to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the web server.


This issue was fixed in commit 89dd3f7.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in SSSD's conversion of X.509 certificate RSA public keys to SSH keys. cna.title: Freeradius: stack-based buffer overflow via unbounded eap-sim identity length

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank s4cr00t (Alipay Security Team) for reporting this issue. Upstream acknowledges Glen Saunders as the original reporter.

workarounds.value:
Disable the EAP-SIM submodule in the FreeRADIUS configuration if SIM-based authentication is not required:

1. Edit `/etc/raddb/mods-available/eap` (or `/etc/raddb/mods-enabled/eap`) and comment out or remove the `sim` configuration block within the `eap` module definition:

```
# sim {
# }
```

2. Restart the FreeRADIUS service to apply the changes:

```
systemctl restart radiusd
```

Warning: Restarting or reloading the FreeRADIUS service will temporarily interrupt active RADIUS authentication requests. Clients relying on EAP-SIM authentication will no longer be able to authenticate.

Additionally, restrict RADIUS UDP traffic (ports 1812 and 1813) to trusted Network Access Server (NAS) IP addresses using firewall rules to limit exposure to untrusted networks.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in freeradius's Extensible Authentication Protocol Method for Subscriber Identity Module (EAP-SIM) module. When handling authentication requests, the server copies a client-supplied identity into an internal structure without properly checking its length against a fixed-size buffer. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by sending specially crafted EAP-SIM messages, triggering a stack buffer overflow that crashes the service and results in a Denial of Service (DoS).

descriptions.value: CAPEC-1

In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment return Submodel Elements that the caller is not authorized to read from `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/submodel-elements`.



If an access rule grants READ on a single Submodel Element through a `$sme` `REFERABLE` object, the list route returns every element of that Submodel, including its value, as soon as one element matches the caller's rules. The single-element route and the full Submodel read enforce the same rule and deny access to the other elements. An authenticated caller with a READ grant for one element of a Submodel can therefore read all other elements of that Submodel.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

descriptions.value: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

cna.title: Privilege Escalation in LMS

descriptions.value: CAPEC-175 Code Inclusion

LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to privilege escalation in the lmsd daemon. The daemon loads the libraries listed in the LMS database without checking that they come from a trusted location. An attacker with access to the web server process or with write access to the LMS database can register a malicious library and trigger a configuration reload, causing lmsd to load and execute it. Because the example systemd unit does not set a separate user, lmsd runs as root, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges.
This issue was fixed in commit 89dd3f7. The lmsd component was removed. For existing installations that use lmsd, the recommended solution is to disable and remove this component.

cna.title: RPC session pool exhausted by unfinished fragmented requests

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 keeps the RPC session that is allocated for a fragment of a request with an unknown activity UUID, without a timeout, when the rest of the request never arrives. A session that does not get an Application Relationship is also kept after the response. Repeated fragments or requests with different activity UUIDs exhaust the available sessions, one UDP packet per session. Once they are exhausted the device no longer answers a Connect request until it is restarted. An unauthenticated attacker with ADJACENT network access can use this to cause a denial of service.

descriptions.description: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

affected.product: Eclipse AAS Model for Java (Eclipse AAS4J)

descriptions.value:
In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.

cna.title: Freeradius: stack buffer overflow via unchecked eap-fast sessionticket length

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank s4cr00t (Alipay Security Team) for reporting this issue. Upstream acknowledges Ada Logics and TristanInSec@gmail.com as the original reporters.

workarounds.value:
Disable the EAP-FAST submodule in the FreeRADIUS configuration, or restrict incoming RADIUS traffic to trusted network access points.

1. Disable EAP-FAST:
In `/etc/raddb/mods-available/eap` (or `/etc/raddb/eap.conf`), comment out the `fast` section within the `eap` configuration block and verify that `default_eap_type` is not set to `fast`.

2. Apply configuration changes:
```
systemctl restart radiusd
```

3. Limit network exposure:
Restrict UDP port 1812 to authorized Network Access Server (NAS) clients using firewalld:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-source=<TRUSTED_IP_OR_SUBNET>
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-port=1812/udp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling EAP-FAST prevents authentication for any network clients that rely exclusively on EAP-FAST. Restricting firewall rules will block traffic from unlisted authenticator sources.

Warning:
Restarting or reloading the radiusd service will temporarily disrupt active RADIUS authentication processing.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in freeradius. An improper length validation in the EAP-FAST module allows a stack-based buffer overflow during session ticket processing. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by sending a specially crafted handshake request, causing the server process to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

cna.title: OpenNMS reflected cross-site scripting in the web UI via request parameters

solutions.value: Upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer.

descriptions.value:
A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in the web user interface of multiple versions of OpenNMS Meridian and Horizon. Several web UI pages copy request parameter values into the HTML response without correct contextual output encoding. A remote attacker can craft a link that runs arbitrary JavaScript in the OpenNMS origin when an authenticated user opens it. The script runs in the victim's browser with the victim's session, so the attacker can read page data and send same-origin requests as the victim. The fix encodes the affected request values. On pages that use AngularJS, the fix also stops client-side template evaluation of the reflected values.



The solution is to upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer. Meridian and Horizon installation instructions state that they are intended for installation within an organization's private networks and should not be directly accessible from the Internet.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Flowise 3.1.4 SSRF Bypass via Custom Function Sandbox

descriptions.value: Flowise through 3.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with chatflows or agentflows create/update permissions to bypass the Custom Function sandbox's SSRF protection by requiring a module subpath inside an allowlisted package, such as axios/dist/node/axios.cjs or node-fetch/lib/index.js, which evades the vm2 mock table and returns an unwrapped HTTP client that skips the checkDenyList validation. Attackers can issue arbitrary GET and POST requests with attacker-controlled bodies via POST /api/v1/node-custom-function to reach loopback and internal-network addresses or the cloud metadata endpoint, enabling network mapping, credential disclosure, and state changes on internal services.

descriptions.value: AppFlowy Cloud through 0.9.64 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace members to upload blobs with unvalidated Content-Type values that are later served inline without a Content-Disposition header or authentication on the retrieval route. credits.value: Andres Poulin Mateos — Drakon Tech Solutions SLU

affected.product: Kadence Security – Password, Two Factor Authentication, and Brute Force Protection

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Kadence Security WordPress Plugin < 10.0.6.1 IPv6 Lockout Bypass

descriptions.value: Kadence Security plugin for WordPress (better-wp-security) before 10.0.6.1 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade per-host login lockouts by exploiting IPv6 address handling in ITSEC_Lib::get_ip(), which keys failed-login counters on the full 128-bit IPv6 address rather than a /64 prefix. Attackers who control a routed IPv6 /64 can send each login attempt from a new address within that prefix, resetting the per-host counter each time to perform password spraying and username enumeration, and can similarly evade the auto_ban_admin immediate ban via address rotation.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-616 Establish Rogue Location

Unverified ownership of the default cluster log location in the EMR module in AWS SDK for pandas (awswrangler) from 1.1.0 before 3.18.0 might allow remote actors to read Amazon EMR cluster logs, including job step output, via a pre-created S3 bucket.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 3.18.0 or later. Users who can't upgrade immediately should pass an explicit log location, or create the default EMR log bucket in their own account in each region they use.

cna.title: GamiPress <= 8.1.3 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) SQL Injection via 'name-1[compare]' Parameter

affected.product: GamiPress – Gamification plugin to reward points, badges & ranks in WordPress, now with AI

descriptions.value: The GamiPress – Gamification plugin to reward points, badges & ranks in WordPress, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'name-1[compare]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires that an administrator has published at least one GamiPress achievement step triggered by a Forminator field-value submission event, as the GamiPress Forminator integration listener is the only path that routes a form submission's raw field array — including the attacker-controlled compare operator — into gamipress_query_logs().

cna.title: OpenNMS argument injection in ad-hoc RRD graphs

solutions.value: Upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer.

descriptions.value:
An argument injection vulnerability exists in the ad-hoc RRD graph feature of multiple versions of OpenNMS Meridian and Horizon. The ad-hoc graph endpoint (GET /graph/graph.png?adhoc=true) copies request parameters into the rrdtool command line without validation. A low-privileged authenticated user (ROLE_USER or ROLE_DASHBOARD) can insert extra rrdtool arguments. An injected --daemon argument makes the server connect to an attacker-chosen address, which is a server-side request forgery. An injected DEF statement reads a local RRD file by absolute path. The command runs through exec with an argument array and no shell, so arbitrary operating system command execution is not possible. The fix validates the ad-hoc graph parameters against allowlists.



The solution is to upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer. Meridian and Horizon installation instructions state that they are intended for installation within an organization's private networks and should not be directly accessible from the Internet.

cna.title: Fragment with another data representation releases an Application Relationship

solutions.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to P-Net 1.0.4 or later.

descriptions.value: P-Net before 1.0.4 releases the Application Relationship of an RPC session, without the abort procedure, when a fragment of a request has another data representation (endianness) than the first fragment of the call. The application is not told that the Application Relationship is gone, the cyclic data stops, and the resources of the Application Relationship are left referencing a cleared structure. Another host can then connect in its place. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can do this with one PDU.

cna.title: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, VFS Mount Policy Bypass via Non-Canonical Paths

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, VFS Mount Policy Bypass via Non-Canonical Paths

descriptions.value: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, contain an improper path equivalence flaw in VirtualFileFactory.canonicalisePath that bypasses mount-level access policy. Authenticated users can supply paths with duplicate separators or dot segments to route operations to a less restrictive parent mount and read or write files the child mount denies.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

cna.title: Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers

descriptions.value: CAPEC-227 Sustained Client Engagement

Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: Out-of-bounds read via unvalidated stream_id in Intel ALH DAI get_properties

descriptions.value:
The Intel ALH digital-audio-interface driver function dai_alh_get_properties() in drivers/dai/intel/alh/alh.c used a caller-supplied int stream_id with no range validation. The value indexes the fixed-size static const uint8_t alh_handshake_map[64] array and scales a FIFO register address, so an out-of-range stream_id produces an out-of-bounds read of one byte at an attacker-chosen signed offset from the array. That byte is written into prop->dma_hs_id and the resulting struct dai_properties is copied back to the caller, leaking it.

dai_get_properties_copy() is a Zephyr __syscall, and its verifier z_vrfy_dai_get_properties_copy() (drivers/dai/dai_handlers.c) validates only the device-object permission and the destination buffer, not stream_id. A user-mode thread that has been granted access to the ALH DAI device object can therefore call the syscall with an arbitrary stream_id, crossing the userspace/kernel sandbox boundary.

The impact is a one-byte-per-call arbitrary-offset kernel information disclosure (and leakage of a computed kernel address via fifo_address); a stream_id that resolves to an unmapped page faults in kernel context, giving a local denial of service. Exploitation requires CONFIG_USERSPACE and device access, making this a local, moderate-severity issue. The fix rejects negative and too-large stream_id values up front and returns NULL, which the copy wrapper maps to -ENOENT.

cna.title: Infinite loop (DoS) in Bluetooth GATT client parsing of Read-By-Type responses with zero data length

descriptions.value:
The Bluetooth host GATT client function parse_read_std_char_desc() in subsys/bluetooth/host/gatt.c parses an ATT Read By Type Response received from a remote GATT server during BT_GATT_DISCOVER_STD_CHAR_DESC discovery. The per-entry stride rsp->len is taken directly from the peer's PDU, and the parse loop both tests its exit condition (length >= rsp->len) and advances (length -= rsp->len, pdu += rsp->len) using that value. The minimum value of rsp->len was never validated before the loop.

A malicious or malfunctioning peer can reply with rsp->len = 0. Because length is unsigned and never decreases, the loop condition stays true forever and the read pointer never advances; as long as the body is at least a few bytes with a non-zero handle and a matching descriptor UUID, the host repeatedly re-parses the same bytes and invokes the discovery callback, never terminating. This hangs the Bluetooth host processing thread (CWE-835, loop with unreachable exit condition).

The condition is reachable by any connected peer once the local device initiates standard-descriptor-value discovery; GATT discovery does not require bonding or encryption, so an unauthenticated adjacent attacker that the device connects to can trigger it. The impact is denial of service of the Bluetooth subsystem (and likely a watchdog reset on constrained targets); there is no memory disclosure or corruption.

The fix adds a rsp->len < sizeof(struct bt_att_data) check before the loop, rejecting under-length responses so the stride is always non-zero and the loop terminates. The sibling parsers parse_include() and parse_characteristic() already validated rsp->len and are unaffected.

cna.title: SAML assertion replay via skipped InResponseTo validation

descriptions.value: When SAML IdP-initiated login is enabled in Grafana Enterprise, the SAML library skips validation of the InResponseTo field on all SAML responses, including SP-initiated logins. This removes anti-replay protection, allowing an attacker who obtains a valid signed SAML assertion to replay it and gain a session as the victim user. affected.product: MultiVendorX – WooCommerce Multivendor Marketplace AI Powered Solutions

descriptions.value: The Dc Woocommerce Multi Vendor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'order_by' parameter of the /multivendorx/v1/compliance/report-abuse REST endpoint in versions up to and including 5.0.18. This is due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query — the value is concatenated directly into an ORDER BY clause where esc_sql() (which only neutralizes characters needed to break out of quoted string literals) provides no protection. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with vendor-level access and above (users granted the 'edit_stores' capability), to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

cna.title: PL011 UART error interrupts never cleared, enabling an external-peer interrupt-storm denial of service

descriptions.value:
The ARM PL011 UART driver in drivers/serial/uart_pl011.c fails to acknowledge receive error interrupts. On the PL011, the framing, parity, break, and overrun error interrupts (PL011_IMSC_ERROR_MASK) are cleared only by writing the interrupt-clear register UARTICR; reading the data register clears the RX interrupt and the per-byte RSR status but not the error interrupt status in MIS. The interrupt service routine pl011_isr() acknowledged only the CTS modem-status interrupt and never wrote icr for the error bits, so an asserted error interrupt remains pending after the ISR returns.

When an application enables error-interrupt reporting via the public uart_irq_err_enable() API, an attacker who controls the serial peer can deterministically assert these error bits by injecting line errors on the RX line — a baud/stop-bit mismatch or mid-character break (framing/break error), a flipped parity bit (parity error), or FIFO flooding (overrun error). Because the error interrupt is never cleared, the interrupt line stays asserted and the CPU re-enters pl011_isr() immediately and indefinitely, producing an interrupt-storm livelock from which the core makes no forward progress.

The impact is an availability-only denial of service (permanent hang), reachable from an external or removable UART peer. Exploitation is gated by configuration: the error interrupt is off by default and no in-tree subsystem enables it, so only applications that explicitly call uart_irq_err_enable() on a PL011-based, interrupt-driven port are affected. The fix makes pl011_isr() acknowledge the pending error bits via uart->icr, breaking the loop, and additionally clears the latched RSR status in pl011_err_check().

cna.title: miniOrange Social Login and Register (Discord, Google, Twitter, LinkedIn) <= 7.7.0 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Administrator Account Takeover via Profile Completion OTP Flow

affected.product: miniOrange Social Login and Register (Discord, Google, Twitter, LinkedIn)

descriptions.value: The miniOrange Social Login and Register (Discord, Google, Twitter, LinkedIn) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authentication bypass leading to account takeover in versions up to and including 7.7.0. This is due to the Profile Completion flow accepting an arbitrary email address via the 'email_field' POST parameter without verifying that the email belongs to the identity returned by the OAuth provider, combined with send_otp_token() returning the SHA-512(customer_key || otp) transaction hash to the client where the OTP space is only 99,000 values (wp_rand(1000, 99999)) and the customer_key is a static option (empty on unregistered installs). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to trigger an OTP email to an arbitrary admin's address, crack the OTP offline from the leaked hash in under a second, and submit the cracked OTP to mo_openid_social_login_validate_otp(), which logs the attacker in as the user whose email was supplied — granting full administrator access.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the cifs-utils package where the cifs.upcall helper fails to securely drop its root privileges before looking up user information inside a user-controlled environment. A local, low privileged attacker can exploit this by using a crafted request_key payload to trick the root-owned helper into entering a custom environment (namespace) containing a malicious NSS module. This forces the system to load the attacker's controlled NSS Module and configuration, allowing them to execute arbitrary commands as the root user, elevating their privileges and fully compromising the system.

workarounds.value:
The following practices would help for avoiding exposure and mitigate this flaw:
- Restrict network egress from controller pods using Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to prevent outbound connections to untrusted destinations. Only allow connections to known Vault server endpoints.
- Review and restrict the RBAC permissions of the automation-controller service account to follow the principle of least privilege. Remove unnecessary secret read access.
- In AAP Cloud environments, audit credential-creation activity for suspicious HashiCorp Vault credentials with external or unusual URLs.
- Monitor Kubernetes audit logs for unexpected API calls using the automation-controller service account, particularly secret reads and pod operations from EE pods.
- Rotate the automation-controller service account token if unauthorized access is suspected.
- Consider restricting the "create credential" privilege to only trusted administrators until the fix is available.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the AAP Controller's HashiCorp Vault credential plugin. The kubernetes_auth() function in awx_plugins/credentials/hashivault.py reads the controller pod's Kubernetes service account token and sends it to an attacker-controlled URL when a HashiCorp Vault Secret Lookup credential with kubernetes_role authentication is tested. An authenticated attacker with credential-creation privileges can exfiltrate the service account token, gaining Kubernetes API access to the control plane namespaces with full pod CRUD and secret read permissions, including database credentials and the Django SECRET_KEY.

cna.title: SQL injection in Amazon Athena Synapse connector

descriptions.value: CAPEC-66 SQL Injection

Amazon Athena is a serverless, interactive query service that lets you analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena Query Federation is a feature that allows you to connect to data sources outside of Amazon S3 like DynamoDB, Azure Synapse, and custom connectors using standard SQL syntax.



Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command in the Synapse connector in Amazon aws-athena-query-federation v2022.20.1 through v2026.19.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to execute injected read-only SQL queries that return unintended data from the connected database via a crafted table name.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version v2026.21.1 or later.

Amazon Athena is a serverless, interactive query service that lets you analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena Query Federation is a feature that allows you to connect to data sources outside of Amazon S3 like DynamoDB, Azure Synapse, and custom connectors using standard SQL syntax.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command in the Synapse connector in Amazon aws-athena-query-federation v2022.20.1 through v2026.19.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to execute injected read-only SQL queries that return unintended data from the connected database via a crafted table name.

To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version v2026.21.1 or later.

cna.title: Arbitrary HDF5 File Read via Virtual Dataset Bypass in keras-team/keras

descriptions.value: Keras versions up to and including 3.13.2 are vulnerable to an arbitrary HDF5 file read due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-1669. The vulnerability resides in the `H5IOStore._verify_dataset()` and `file_editor.py` methods, which fail to check the `dataset.is_virtual` property of HDF5 datasets. This allows an attacker to craft a malicious `.keras` model archive or `.h5` weights file containing a Virtual Dataset (VDS) that references external HDF5 files on the victim's filesystem. When the victim loads the model using `keras.models.load_model()` or `keras.saving.load_model()`, the external file is transparently read, leading to potential information disclosure. Fixed in versions 3.12.2 and 3.14.1.

descriptions.value: syracom AG Secure Login (2FA) for Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Bitbucket 3.4.0.x contains an authentication bypass vulnerability. An attacker with valid credentials for a user account can bypass the two-factor authentication flow by sending HTTP requests with a crafted User-Agent header containing specific strings such as AtlassianMobileApp or JIRA. When such a User-Agent is present, the plugin does not enforce the configured 2FA checks for protected web resources. Successful exploitation allows the attacker to access the affected Atlassian application as the compromised user without completing 2FA. If the compromised account has administrative privileges, the attacker can access administrative functionality and may disable the 2FA plugin or make arbitrary administrative changes. The issue is fixed in version 3.5.0.0.

cna.title: Denial of Service via HDF5 Shape Bomb in keras.models.load_model() in keras-team/keras

descriptions.value: A vulnerability in keras-team/keras versions <= 3.15.0 allows for a denial of service (DoS) attack when loading malicious .keras model files via the keras.models.load_model() function. The H5IOStore.__getitem__ method in keras/src/saving/saving_lib.py does not validate the shape or size of datasets, leading to unbounded memory allocation. A specially crafted .keras file can exploit this flaw to trigger an out-of-memory (OOM) condition, causing the process to be terminated (exit code 137). This issue bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-0897, which only addressed a similar vulnerability in KerasFileEditor. The attack vector includes poisoned models from public repositories or malicious model registries, posing a risk to machine learning pipelines that process untrusted models.

affected.product: Cookie Banner for GDPR / CCPA – WPLP Cookie Consent

descriptions.value: The GDPR Cookie Consent plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data due to a missing capability check and missing nonce verification on the gdpr_cookie_consent_ajax_save_schedule_scan() function (the wp_ajax_gcc_save_schedule_scan AJAX action) in versions up to, and including, 4.3.6. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to modify the plugin's cookie scan schedule configuration stored in the gdpr_scan_schedule_data option, which is an administrative function intended to be limited to users with the manage_options capability.

cna.title: Socket versions before 2.041 for Perl have an out-of-bounds heap read

solutions.value: Upgrade to version 2.041 or later.

descriptions.value:
Socket versions before 2.041 for Perl have an out-of-bounds heap read.

In Socket.xs, pack_ip_mreq_source() checks the length of its source argument before the argument is read, so the check tests the byte length carried over from the preceding multiaddr argument instead. Both addresses occupy a 4-byte field, so a valid multiaddr lets a source of any length pass the check, and the source is then copied into the 4-byte imr_sourceaddr field with a fixed-size copy. A source shorter than 4 bytes is not rejected, and the copy reads up to 3 bytes past the end of its buffer.

Calling pack_ip_mreq_source() with a source value shorter than 4 bytes copies adjacent heap memory into the returned packed structure.

descriptions.description: CWE-805 Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value

cna.title: TOCTOU double-fetch in `zsock_sendmsg`/`recvmsg` userspace verifiers allows kernel-heap out-of-bounds write

descriptions.value:
The userspace syscall verifiers z_vrfy_zsock_sendmsg() and z_vrfy_zsock_recvmsg() in subsys/net/lib/sockets/sockets.c snapshot the caller-supplied struct net_msghdr into a kernel-side copy with k_usermode_from_copy(), but then re-read the still-live user struct for subsequent decisions. The kernel iovec shadow buffer is sized from one read of msg->msg_iovlen, while the population loop is bounded by a second, live read of the same field.

Because msg points into ordinary user memory, a cooperating second thread in the same memory domain can inflate msg->msg_iovlen in the window between the sizing read and the loop test (a classic double-fetch / TOCTOU). The population loop then iterates past the number of net_iovec slots actually allocated, writing attacker-influenced iov_base/iov_len values beyond the end of the kernel-heap shadow buffer. The recvmsg verifier has the same defect on both its inbound and result write-back loops.

The code is reachable from an unprivileged user thread whenever CONFIG_USERSPACE is enabled and the zsock_sendmsg/zsock_recvmsg syscalls are available. A successful race corrupts kernel-managed heap memory across the user-to-kernel privilege boundary, yielding a local privilege-escalation primitive or, at minimum, a kernel-fault denial of service. The fix copies the header once and derives every size, bound, and gate from the snapshot, copying each iovec entry atomically so its base and length can no longer be raced apart.

affected.product: Stripe Payment Forms by WP Full Pay – Accept Credit Card Payments, Donations & Subscriptions

descriptions.value: The WP Full Stripe Free plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in versions up to, and including, 8.4.3 via the wpfs_update_failed_payment_status AJAX action. The handler is registered through both wp_ajax_ and wp_ajax_nopriv_ hooks and the underlying update_failed_payment_status() function performs no capability check, no nonce verification, and no logged-in check before calling $this->db->updatePaymentByEventId() with attacker-controlled POST parameters. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who can obtain a valid Stripe Payment Intent ID for the target site (Payment Intent IDs are exposed to the customer browser during normal Stripe.js checkout flows) to manipulate payment records in the site's database, marking previously successful payments as failed and overwriting failure codes and messages with attacker-supplied values.

AvastSvc denial of service via unhandled JsonCpp exceptions in native message handlers

credits.value: Teng Zheng Wang by VulnGuard Labs

descriptions.value: A local, unprivileged attacker can crash AvastSvc by sending specially crafted JSON via native message handlers, resulting in temporary denial of service, antivirus protection disruption, and repeated service restart churn.

affected.product: Avast Antivirus, Avast One, Avast Premium Security, Avast Ultimate, Avast Business Security
AVG Antivirus Free, AVG Internet Security, AVG Ultimate
Norton Antivirus Plus, Norton 360 Standard, Norton 360 Deluxe, Norton 360 Advanced

solutions.value:
Gen Digital has released a fix in Avast, AVG, and Norton version 26.7 and later. The fix adds exception handlers around JSON type conversions in the native message dispatcher, catching and safely logging JsonCpp exceptions instead of allowing them to propagate and crash the service. The fix addresses all three vulnerable code paths simultaneously.



Upgrade to version 26.7 or later to remediate this issue.

descriptions.value:
Missing exception handlers in AvastSvc native message dispatcher (ashServ.dll) on Windows allow a local, unprivileged attacker to crash the service by sending specially crafted JSON messages.



The vulnerability spans multiple handler pathways in the RPC-based native message protocol:

  *  Log_NmSvc.message handler: converts JSON fields to strings without type validation and without exception boundaries. 
  *  OpenInSz_NmSvc handler: converts URL and origin fields to strings without type checking, exposing an exception.
  *  OpenInSz_NmSvc.profile handler: converts the profile field to an integer without validation.


In all three cases, the exceptions are not caught by action-specific handlers and propagate up the dispatcher. The common root cause is the absence of try-catch blocks around JSON type conversions in the native message processing chain.

The vulnerability spans multiple handler pathways in the RPC-based native message protocol:

  2. OpenInSz_NmSvc handler: converts URL and origin fields to strings without type checking, exposing an exception.
  3. OpenInSz_NmSvc.profile handler: converts the profile field to an integer without validation.

In all three cases, the exceptions are not caught by action-specific handlers and propagate up the dispatcher. The common root cause is the absence of try-catch blocks around JSON type conversions in the native message processing chain.

cna.title: Uncontrolled memory usage in Innodata Labs’ Poppler JPX decoder

solutions.value:
No fix has been reported as yet for the fork maintained by Innodata Labs.



Meanwhile, Poppler has removed the JPX decoder code.

supportingMedia.value:
No fix has been reported as yet for the fork maintained by Innodata Labs.

Meanwhile, Poppler has removed the JPX decoder code.

descriptions.value: Denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability in the internal JPEG2000 (JPX) decoding implementation of the Poppler fork developed by Innodata Labs. When an application processes an untrusted PDF file containing specially crafted JPXDecode images, a remote attacker can cause uncontrolled memory consumption. The flaw occurs in the JPXStream::readCodestream() function, where values controlled from the SIZ segment (such as img.nComps) are used for the memory allocation of tiles and components without adequate validation. This allows an attacker to force excessive memory allocation and cause a resource exhaustion, ultimately causing the pdftoppm process to terminate due to out-of-memory (OOM) conditions.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-554 Functionality Bypass

Docker Sandboxes (sbx) enforces an HTTP/S-only egress allowlist but does not apply it to DNS resolution: the per-network embedded DNS server forwards any queried name to the host resolver whenever the network is internet-connected, without consulting the policy. A workload inside a sandbox, which the threat model treats as untrusted, can therefore encode data into DNS labels for an attacker-controlled domain and exfiltrate it through a DNS covert channel, bypassing the configured allowlist.

cna.title: Uninitialized mutex in TLS trusted-credential backend causes kernel NULL-deref DoS under contention

descriptions.value:
The PSA Protected Storage credential backend (subsys/net/lib/tls_credentials/tls_credentials_trusted.c) declared its credential-store mutex as a plain zero-filled static struct k_mutex credential_lock; and never called k_mutex_init() on it. A statically zero-filled k_mutex has an uninitialized wait queue (its dlist head/tail are NULL instead of the self-referential sentinels that k_mutex_init/K_MUTEX_DEFINE install). The uncontended lock path does not touch the wait queue, so the defect is latent and serialized use behaves correctly.

When two execution contexts contend on the lock, k_mutex_lock() pends the blocking thread on the wait queue via z_pend_curr(), which calls sys_dlist_append() on the zeroed list and dereferences a NULL tail pointer (tail->next = node), faulting the kernel. The lock is held during TLS handshake credential loading and by all credential add/get/delete operations, so a deployment performing concurrent TLS handshakes (for example a server handling multiple simultaneous connections from a remote peer) or a credential-management operation concurrent with a handshake can trigger the dereference.

The impact is a denial of service: a deterministic kernel panic / device reset on the first contention. There is no memory corruption beyond the NULL dereference and no confidentiality or integrity impact; mutual exclusion on the fast path remains correct. Exposure is limited to builds with CONFIG_TLS_CREDENTIALS_BACKEND_PROTECTED_STORAGE enabled (PSA Protected Storage / TF-M platforms); the default volatile RAM backend initializes its lock correctly and is unaffected.

The fix initializes the mutex statically with K_MUTEX_DEFINE(credential_lock), providing a valid wait queue so the contended path no longer touches a NULL list.

Upon receiving a UDP message,  the server reads at most 1460 bytes into a local buffer and a pointer to the buffer is stored in a global variable:

      v3 = strlen(g_network_config->ip_addr);
